_comment: Full per-CORE libretro option catalog for the arcade per-game config module. Tokens are the cores' EXACT values (validation allowlist) — do not hand-edit. GENERATED by scripts/extract-core-options (runtime harness; driver scripts/extract-core-options.ps1) from the DEPLOYED core DLLs in D:/ArcadeStorage/worker-gl/assets/cores. Per-core disposition (fold vs hand-only) lives in scripts/extract-core-options/policy.json; hand-only cores are catalogued in ArcadeCoreOptionCatalog.cs instead and deliberately absent here. Renderer-selecting keys ARE present under 'cores' and are filtered at fold time by LoadExtracted; 'rendererKeys' is the sidecar every deployed core's renderer tokens (incl. hand-only cores) so RenderProfile.Options can be validated against real tokens.

options.label: CPU Frequency Scaling (Overclock)
options.desc: Overclock (or underclock) the emulated PSX CPU. Overclocking can eliminate slowdown and improve frame rates in certain games at the expense of increased performance requirements. Note that some games have an internal frame rate limiter and may not benefit from overclocking. May cause certain effects to animate faster than intended in some titles when overclocked.

options.label: GPU Rasterizer Overclock
options.desc: Enable overclocking of the 2D rasterizer contained within the emulated PSX's GPU. Does not improve 3D rendering, and in general has little effect.

options.label: GTE Overclock
options.desc: Lower all emulated GTE (CPU coprocessor for 3D graphics) operations to a constant one-cycle latency. For games that make heavy use of the GTE, this can greatly improve frame rate and frame time stability.

options.label: CD Access Method
options.desc: 'Synchronous' mimics original hardware. 'Asynchronous' can reduce stuttering on devices with slow storage. 'Pre-Cache' loads the entire disk image into memory when launching content, which may improve in-game loading times at the cost of an initial delay at startup. 'Pre-Cache' may cause issues on systems with low RAM, and will fall back to 'Synchronous' for physical media. Restart required.

options.label: CD Loading Speed
options.desc: Values higher than '2x (Native)' can greatly reduce in-game loading times, but may introduce timing errors. Some games may not function properly above a certain value.

options.label: Skip BIOS
options.desc: Skip the PlayStation BIOS boot animation normally displayed when loading content. Note: Enabling this causes compatibility issues with a number of games (PAL copy protected games, Saga Frontier, etc.).

options.label: Override BIOS
options.desc: Override the standard region specific BIOS with a region-free one if found. Restart required.

options.label: System Region
options.desc: Sets the fallback region used when content cannot be auto-detected (e.g. raw PS-X EXE files). Disc-based games still use the region embedded on the disc. Restart required.

options.label: Internal GPU Resolution
options.desc: Resolutions higher than '1x (Native)' improve fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

options.label: Renderer
options.desc: The software renderer is the most accurate but has steep performance requirements when running at increased internal GPU resolutions. The hardware renderers, while less accurate, improve performance over the software renderer at increased internal resolutions and enable various graphical enhancements. 'Hardware (Auto)' automatically selects the Vulkan or OpenGL renderer, depending upon the current libretro frontend video driver. If the provided video driver is not Vulkan or OpenGL 3.3-compatible, then the core will fall back to the software renderer. Restart required.

options.label: Software Framebuffer
options.desc: Enable accurate emulation of framebuffer effects (e.g. motion blur, FF7 battle swirl) when using hardware renderers by running a copy of the software renderer at native resolution in the background. If disabled, these operations are omitted (OpenGL) or rendered on the GPU (Vulkan). Disabling can improve performance but may cause severe graphical errors. Leave enabled if unsure.

options.label: Internal Color Depth
options.desc: Higher color depth can reduce color banding effects without the use of dithering. 16 bpp emulates original hardware but may have visible banding if dithering is not enabled. 'Dithering Pattern' is recommended to be disabled when this option is set to 32 bpp.

options.label: Dithering Pattern
options.desc: '1x (Native)' emulates native low resolution dithering used by original hardware to smooth out color banding artifacts visible at native color depth. 'Internal Resolution' scales dithering granularity to the configured internal resolution for cleaner results. Recommended to be disabled when running at 32 bpp color depth. Note: On Vulkan, enabling this will force downsampling to native color depth, while disabling will automatically enable output at higher color depth.

options.label: Texture UV Offset
options.desc: Sample textures for 3D polygons at an offset for higher than 1x internal resolution. Reduces texture seams but may cause unintended graphical glitches.

options.label: Texture Filtering
options.desc: 'Nearest' emulates original hardware. 'Bilinear' and '3-Point' are smoothing filters, which reduce pixelation via blurring. 'SABR', 'xBR', and 'JINC2' are upscaling filters that may improve texture fidelity/sharpness at the expense of increased performance requirements. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

options.label: Exclude Sprites from Filtering
options.desc: Do not apply texture filtering to sprites. Prevents seams in various games with 2D sprite-rendered backgrounds. Use together with Adaptive Smoothing or another post-processing filter for best effect.

options.label: Exclude 2D Polygons from Filtering
options.desc: Do not apply texture filtering to 2D polygons. 2D polygons are detected with a heuristic and there may be glitches. Use together with Adaptive Smoothing or another post-processing filter for best effect.

options.label: Adaptive Smoothing
options.desc: Smooth out 2D artwork and UI elements without blurring 3D rendered objects. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer.

options.label: Supersampling (Downsample to Native Resolution)
options.desc: Downsample rendered content from upscaled internal resolution down to native resolution. Combining this with higher internal resolution multipliers allows for games to be displayed with anti-aliased 3D objects at native low resolution. Produces best results when applied to titles that mix 2D and 3D elements (e.g. 3D characters on pre-rendered backgrounds), and works well in conjunction with CRT shaders. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer. Note: 'Dithering Pattern' is recommended to be disabled when enabling this option.

options.label: Multi-Sampled Anti Aliasing
options.desc: MSAA improves the appearance of 3D objects. Only supported by the Vulkan renderer.

options.label: MDEC YUV Chroma Filter
options.desc: Improve the quality of FMV playback by reducing 'macroblocking' artifacts (squares/jagged edges). Only supported by the Vulkan renderer.

options.label: Track Textures
options.desc: Prerequisite for texture dumping and replacement. Will probably crash in most games.

options.label: Dump Textures
options.desc: Dump used textures to <cd>-texture-dump/

options.label: HD Dump Mode
options.desc: How dumped textures are laid out (experimental). 'Upload-rect' (default) dumps each tracked upload to <cd>-texture-dump/ (matches stock Beetle). 'Page-aligned' dumps whole VRAM texture pages to <cd>-texture-dump-pages/ for cleaner tiles. 'Both' dumps to both folders simultaneously, so a single playthrough collects both pack types (folders stay separate; pick which to edit afterwards). Page packs are NOT interchangeable with upload-rect packs (the hash covers a different region).

options.label: Replace Textures
options.desc: Replace textures using HD versions from <cd>-texture-replacements/

options.label: HD Texture Folder
options.desc: Where texture dump and replacement folders are kept. 'Content directory' (default) keeps them next to the game image (current behaviour). 'System directory' / 'Save directory' put them under RetroArch's configured System or Save folder instead - one central location for every game's packs (set those paths in Settings > Directory). Each game still gets its own '<name>-texture-dump' / '-replacements' subfolder, so games never collide. Changing this re-scans replacements from the new folder.

options.label: HD Replacement Mode
options.desc: Where replacement textures are looked up (experimental). 'Upload-rect' (default) matches per-upload textures from <cd>-texture-replacements/ (matches stock Beetle). 'Page-aligned' matches whole VRAM pages from <cd>-texture-replacements-pages/. Independent of HD Dump Mode; page packs are NOT interchangeable with upload-rect packs.

options.label: HD Replacement Cross-Mode Fallback
options.desc: On an HD texture miss in the active HD Replacement Mode, also check the OTHER mode's folder before falling back to native. Works both ways: an upload-rect pack can fill gaps from a page-aligned pack and vice-versa, without converting packs. Best with the Lazy caching method.

options.label: HD Reduce Palette Range
options.desc: Opt-in. When dumping/replacing HD textures, hash only the palette (CLUT) entries the texture actually uses instead of the whole CLUT. This makes a texture's hash ignore unused palette entries that games often leave as garbage or rewrite over time, so one replacement keeps matching across those variations - fewer dumps and far better match coverage (most useful for 8bpp textures). Filenames are unchanged in format and remain loadable; old full-palette packs still match with this enabled (the matcher falls back to the full-palette hash when no reduced file is present). Applies to both the upload-rect and page-aligned paths. Re-dump a game to benefit.

options.label: HD Texture Caching Method
options.desc: How HD replacement textures are loaded. 'Eager' prefetches all palette variants of a texture when it is uploaded (matches stock Beetle). 'Lazy' loads each texture+palette only when first drawn, in the background (leaner; brief pop-in possible on first use). 'Lazy (synchronous)' also loads on first use but blocks the renderer until ready (no pop-in, but may briefly stutter when many new textures appear at once). Both use the VRAM/RAM caches and budgets below.

options.label: HD Texture VRAM Cache Budget
options.desc: Maximum VRAM used to keep uploaded HD replacement textures resident. Higher keeps more textures ready (smoother) but can exhaust VRAM on smaller GPUs and cause slowdown; lower it if you see stutter. Only used with Replace Textures.

options.label: HD Texture RAM Cache Budget
options.desc: Maximum system RAM used to keep decoded HD replacement textures, so they don't have to be re-read from disk. Only used with Replace Textures.

options.label: PGXP Operation Mode
options.desc: Render 3D objects with subpixel precision, minimizing distortion and jitter of 3D objects seen on original hardware due to the usage of fixed point vertex coordinates. 'Memory Only' mode has minimal compatibility issues and is recommended for general use. 'Memory + CPU (Buggy)' mode can reduce jitter even further but has high performance requirements and may cause various geometry errors.

options.label: PGXP 2D Geometry Tolerance
options.desc: Hide more glaring errors in PGXP operations: the value specifies the tolerance in which PGXP values will be kept in case of geometries without proper depth information.

options.label: PGXP Primitive Culling
options.desc: Use PGXP's NCLIP implementation. Improves appearance by reducing holes in geometries with PGXP coordinates. Known to cause some games to lock up in various circumstances.

options.label: PGXP Vertex Cache
options.desc: Cache PGXP-enhanced vertex positions for re-use across polygon draws. Can potentially improve object alignment and reduce visible seams when rendering textures, but false positives when querying the cache may produce graphical glitches. It is currently recommended to leave this option disabled. This option is applied only when PGXP Operation Mode is enabled. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

options.label: PGXP Perspective Correct Texturing
options.desc: Replace native PSX affine texture mapping with perspective correct texture mapping. Eliminates position-dependent distortion and warping of textures, resulting in properly aligned textures. This option is applied only when PGXP Operation Mode is enabled. Supported by the hardware renderers and the software renderer.

options.label: Display Internal FPS
options.desc: Display the internal frame rate at which the emulated PlayStation system is rendering content. Note: Requires onscreen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

options.label: Display OSD Messages
options.desc: Display OSD messages generated by the core.

options.label: Display Full VRAM (Debug)
options.desc: Visualize the entire emulated console's VRAM. Only supported by the OpenGL and Vulkan hardware renderers. Note: This is for debugging purposes, and should normally be disabled.

options.label: Analog Self-Calibration
options.desc: Enable dynamic calibration of analog inputs when the device is set to DualShock, Analog Controller, Analog Joystick, or neGcon. Maximum registered input values are monitored in real time and used to scale analog coordinates passed to the emulator. This should be used for games such as Mega Man Legends 2 that expect larger values than what modern controllers provide. For best results, analog sticks should be rotated at full extent to tune the calibration algorithm each time content is loaded.

options.label: DualShock Analog Mode Toggle
options.desc: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. Mode can also be toggled by using the selected button combination.

options.label: DualShock Analog Mode Combo

values.label: L1 + L2 + R1 + R2 + Start + Select

options.desc: The button combination that will be used to toggle between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode for the emulated DualShock.

options.label: DualShock Analog Mode Combo Hold Delay
options.desc: Hold time for the analog mode combo buttons.

options.label: Multitap on Port 1
options.desc: Enable multitap functionality on port 1.

options.label: Multitap on Port 2
options.desc: Enable multitap functionality on port 2.

options.label: Gun Input Mode
options.desc: Use mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input when device type is set to 'Guncon/G-Con 45' or 'Justifier'.

options.label: Gun Cursor
options.desc: Draw a cursor on screen while using the 'Guncon/G-Con 45' and 'Justifier' input device types.

options.label: Gun Crosshair Color: Port 1
options.desc: Light gun crosshair color for port 1.

options.label: Gun Crosshair Color: Port 2
options.desc: Light gun crosshair color for port 2.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.desc: Responsiveness of the 'Mouse' input device type.

options.label: neGcon Twist Response
options.desc: Left analog stick response type when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Analog stick displacement may be mapped to neGcon rotation angle either linearly, quadratically or cubically. 'Quadratic' allows for greater precision than 'Linear' when making small movements. 'Cubic' further increases small movement precision, but 'exaggerates' larger movements. Note: 'Linear' is only recommended when using racing wheel peripherals. Conventional controllers implement analog input in a manner fundamentally different from the neGcon 'twist' mechanism, such that linear mapping over-amplifies small movements, impairing fine control. In most cases, 'Quadratic' provides the closest approximation of real hardware.

options.label: neGcon Twist Deadzone
options.desc: Left analog stick deadzone when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated 'neGcon' input devices. Used to eliminate controller drift. Note: Most neGcon-compatible titles provide in-game options for setting a 'twist' deadzone value. To avoid loss of precision, the in-game deadzone should *always* be set to zero. Any required adjustments should *only* be applied via this core option. This is particularly important when 'neGcon Twist Response' is set to 'Quadratic' or 'Cubic'.

options.label: Memory Card Method
options.desc: Save data format used for the left memory card slot. 'Mednafen' may be used for compatibility with the stand-alone version of Mednafen. When used with Beetle PSX, Libretro (.srm) and Mednafen (.mcr) saves have internally identical formats and can be converted between one another via renaming. Restart required.

options.label: Memory Card Slot 2
options.desc: Emulate a second memory card in the right memory card slot. Note: Some games require this option to be disabled for correct operation (e.g. Codename Tenka). Note: Memory Card Slot 2 uses the Mednafen (.mcr) save format. Restart required.

options.label: Shared Memory Cards
options.desc: Use shared memory cards instead of separate cards for each content. Note: if 'Memory Card Method' is set to 'Libretro', only memory card slot 2 will be affected. Restart required.

options.label: Memory Card Slot 1 Index
options.desc: Memory card currently loaded in the left slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Method is set to Mednafen.

options.label: Memory Card Slot 2 Index
options.desc: Memory card currently loaded in the right slot. This option will only work if Memory Card Slot 2 is enabled.

options.label: Line-to-Quad Hack
options.desc: Some games (e.g. Doom, Hexen, Soul Blade, etc.) draw horizontal lines by stretching single-pixel-high triangles across the screen, which are rasterized as a row of pixels on original hardware. This hack detects these small triangles and converts them to quads as required, allowing them to be displayed properly on the hardware renderers and at upscaled internal resolutions. 'Aggressive' is required for some titles (e.g. Dark Forces, Duke Nukem) but may otherwise introduce graphical glitches. Leave at 'Default' if unsure.

options.label: Widescreen Mode Hack
options.desc: Render 3D content anamorphically and output the emulated framebuffer at a widescreen aspect ratio. Produces best results with fully 3D games. 2D elements will be horizontally stretched and may be misaligned.

options.label: Widescreen Mode Hack Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Aspect ratio to be used by the Widescreen Mode Hack.

options.label: SPU Silent Voice Optimization
options.desc: Skip the per-sample processing of voices whose envelope has fully released. Audio output is identical; the optimization automatically disables itself while the SPU IRQ is in use. Saves roughly 5-10% of frame time. Disable for fully accurate SPU register state.

options.label: CPU Dynarec
options.desc: Dynamically recompile CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than interpreter, but CPU timing is less accurate, and may have bugs.

options.label: Dynarec Code Invalidation
options.desc: Some games require 'Full' invalidation, some require 'DMA Only'.

options.label: Dynarec Cycles Per Instruction
options.desc: Cycles the dynarec charges per CPU instruction. '2' is faster, but the emulated CPU appears half-speed to games that pace themselves against it - set '1' for games whose CD streaming stalls or hangs under the dynarec (e.g. Parasite Eve 2). The '1' setting charges memory accesses two cycles and everything else one, close to the real CPU.

options.label: Dynarec DMA/GPU/MDEC/Timer Event Cycles
options.desc: Max cycles run by CPU before a GPU/DMA/MDEC/Timer Update is checked, higher number will be faster, has much less impact on beetle interpreter than dynarec.

options.label: Dynarec SPU Samples
options.desc: Max SPU samples to run before a SPU Update is checked, higher number will be faster, but will cause sound glitches in some games with anything other than 1.

options.label: Dynarec SP GP Hit RAM Optimization
options.desc: Enabled will generate faster code, but potentially crash, by assuming sp and gp registers always point to ram, disabled is more widely compatible

options.label: Core-Reported FPS Timing
options.desc: Automatic Toggling allows the core to switch between progressive and interlaced rates.

options.label: Deinterlace Method
options.desc: 'Weave' shows both fields on the same frame for full high resolution still image, 'Bob' sacrificies resolution clarity for motion clarity. 'Bob (Offset)' is Bob with the current field doubled into the full surface height with a one-line offset between fields, preserving the libretro output resolution while keeping Bob-style smooth motion. 'FastMAD (Motion Adaptive)' weaves still pixels and vertically-interpolates moving pixels per-pixel, full output height with neither weave's comb on motion nor bob's halved resolution. 'Off' makes the software renderer match the hardware (Vulkan/OpenGL) renderer behaviour by rasterising to all VRAM lines every frame and deferring scanout to the end of the frame, eliminating comb-on-motion in interlaced games. Note: programs that DMA to VRAM during scanout (some demos using >512-line PAL framebuffer-wrap tricks), or that update moving sprites via CPU-to-VRAM image transfers tied to the displayed field (e.g. Pro Pinball), may show stale rows or sprite ghosting under 'Off'; use 'Weave', 'Bob', 'Bob (Offset)', or 'FastMAD' for those.

options.label: Frame Duping
options.desc: Repeat the previous frame if the core has nothing new to display.

options.label: PAL Video Timing Override
options.desc: Due to different standards, PAL games often appear slowed down compared to the American or Japanese NTSC releases. This option can be used to override PAL timings in order to attempt to run these games with the NTSC framerate.

options.label: Core Aspect Ratio
options.desc: This setting is ignored when the Widescreen Mode Hack or Display Full VRAM options are enabled.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.desc: Full native image or no borders.

options.label: Additional Cropping
options.desc: Reduce the width of the cropped image by the specified number of pixels.

options.label: Offset Cropped Image
options.desc: Offset horizontally to the right (positive) or left (negative) by the specified number of pixels. May be used to correct alignment issues. Only supported by the software renderer.

options.label: Horizontal Image Offset (GPU Cycles)
options.desc: Positive values move image to the right, negative values move image to the left. Only supported by the hardware renderers.

options.label: Initial Scan Line - NTSC
options.desc: First displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

options.label: Last Scan Line - NTSC
options.desc: Last displayed scan line when running NTSC content. Values less than 239 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

options.label: Initial Scan Line - PAL
options.desc: First displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values greater than zero will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the topmost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

options.label: Last Scan Line - PAL
options.desc: Last displayed scan line when running PAL content. Values below 287 will reduce the height of output images by cropping pixels from the bottommost edge. May be used to counteract letterboxing.

options.desc: Enable performance queiries.

options.label: Wiimote Default Device
options.desc: Selects the default host input device emulating the Wii Remote for Wii games.

options.label: Sideways Toggle Button
options.desc: Button used to toggle sideways mode. Can be disabled.

options.label: Wiimote IR Mode
options.desc: Control method for Wiimote pointer.

options.label: Wiimote IR Vertical Offset
options.desc: Adjust vertical center of Wiimote pointer.

options.label: Wiimote IR Total Yaw
options.desc: Horizontal field of view for Wiimote pointer.

options.label: Wiimote IR Total Pitch
options.desc: Vertical field of view for Wiimote pointer.

options.label: IR Deadzone
options.desc: Amount of small IR-cursor movement to ignore (0-50%).

options.label: IR Modifier Button
options.desc: Button used as a modifier for IR control. With no modifier selected, IR is always active with right thumbstick.

options.label: Swing Modifier Button
options.desc: Button to hold while using right thumbstick to activate swing. OFF turns off swing. Selecting none will allow free use of right thumb stick to swing (It will automatically filter out L3).

options.label: Swing Angle
options.desc: Rotation applied at the extremities of a swing (1-180°).

options.label: Automatically Import Cheats into RetroArch
options.desc: Import dolphin ini files into RetroArch. Restart core to take effect.

options.label: Load & Prevent Save Settings
options.desc: Choose whether to load core settings from GCPad.ini/WiimoteNew.ini and also prevent saving to them. Core options may no longer be reflected correctly in RetroArch interface. Editing ini files incorrectly will likely crash the emulator.

options.label: Enable Virtual File System (VFS)
options.desc: Enable VFS for SAF/SMB etc. Requires core RESTART. This feature is NEW and EXPERIMENTAL. Backup your saves regularly.

options.label: Force Output FPS
options.desc:
Enable this to force output at a fixed rate. Try 60 FPS if you encounter screen tearing or vsync issues.
Output will have frames skipped at lower rates and frames duplicated at higher rates.

options.label: Save States Support
options.desc:
Make sure to test it in each game before using it. Complex late era DOS games might have problems.
Be aware that states saved with different video, CPU or memory settings are not loadable.
Rewind support comes at a high performance cost and needs at least 40MB of rewind buffer.

options.label: Advanced > Use Strict Mode
options.desc: Disable the command line, running installed operating systems and using .BAT/.COM/.EXE/DOS.YML files from the save game.

options.label: Advanced > Loading of dosbox.conf

values.label: Try 'dosbox.conf' in the loaded content (ZIP or folder)
Try '.conf' with same name as loaded content (next to ZIP or folder)

options.desc: DOSBox Pure is meant to be configured via core options but optionally supports loading of legacy .conf files.

options.label: Advanced > Start Menu

values.label: Show at start, show again after game exit (default)
Show at start, shut down core 5 seconds after auto started game exit
Show at start, shut down core 3 seconds after auto started game exit
Show at start, shut down core immediately after auto started game exit
Always show menu on startup and after game exit, ignore auto start setting

options.desc:
Set the behavior of the start menu before and after launching a game.
You can also force it to open by holding shift or L2/R2 when selecting 'Restart'.

options.label: Advanced > Menu Transparency
options.desc: Set the transparency level of the Menu and the On-Screen Keyboard.

options.label: Use L3 Button to Show Menu

values.label: On (Only On-Screen Keyboard While in Game)

options.desc: Always bind the L3 controller button to show the menu to swap CDs/Disks and use the On-Screen Keyboard.

options.label: Mouse Input Mode

values.label: Direct controlled mouse (not supported by all games)
Touchpad mode (see description, best for touch screens)

options.desc:
You can disable input handling from a mouse or a touchscreen (emulated mouse through joypad will still work).
In touchpad mode use drag to move, tap to click, two finger tap to right-click and press-and-hold to drag

options.label: Bind Mouse Wheel To Key
options.desc: Bind mouse wheel up and down to two keyboard keys to be able to use it in DOS games.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.desc: Sets the overall mouse cursor movement speed.

options.label: Advanced > Horizontal Mouse Sensitivity
options.desc: Experiment with this value if the mouse is too fast/slow when moving left/right.

options.label: Advanced > Action Wheel Inputs
options.desc: Sets which inputs control the action wheel.

options.label: Advanced > Automatic Game Pad Mappings

values.label: Enable with notification on game detection

options.desc:
DOSBox Pure can automatically apply a gamepad control mapping scheme when it detects a game.
These button mappings are provided by the Keyb2Joypad Project (by Jemy Murphy and bigjim).

options.label: Advanced > Keyboard Layout
options.desc: Select the keyboard layout (will not change the On-Screen Keyboard).

options.label: Advanced > Joystick Analog Deadzone
options.desc: Set the deadzone of the joystick analog sticks. May be used to eliminate drift caused by poorly calibrated joystick hardware.

options.label: Advanced > Enable Joystick Timed Intervals
options.desc: Enable timed intervals for joystick axes. Experiment with this option if your joystick drifts.

options.label: Emulated Performance

values.label: AUTO - DOSBox will try to detect performance needs (default)
MAX - Emulate as many instructions as possible

options.desc: The raw performance that DOSBox will try to emulate.

options.label: Detailed > Maximum Emulated Performance
options.desc: With dynamic CPU speed (AUTO or MAX above), the maximum emulated performance level.

options.label: Detailed > Performance Scale
options.desc: Fine tune the emulated performance for specific needs.

options.label: Detailed > Limit CPU Usage
options.desc:
When emulating DOS as fast as possible, how much time per frame should be used by the emulation.
Lower this if your device becomes hot while using this core.

options.label: Advanced > Show Performance Statistics
options.desc: Enable this to show statistics about performance and framerate and check if emulation runs at full speed.

options.label: Emulated Graphics Chip (restart required)
options.desc: The type of graphics chip that DOSBox will emulate.

options.label: CGA Mode
options.desc: The CGA variation that is being emulated.

options.label: Hercules Color Mode
options.desc: The color scheme for Hercules emulation.

options.label: SVGA Mode (restart required)

values.label: S3 Trio64 no-line buffer hack (reduces flickering in some games)

options.desc: The SVGA variation that is being emulated. Try changing this if you encounter graphical glitches.

options.label: SVGA Memory (restart required)
options.desc: The amount of memory available to the emulated SVGA card.

options.label: 3dfx Voodoo Emulation
options.desc:
Enables certain games with support for the Voodoo 3D accelerator.
3dfx Voodoo Graphics SST-1/2 emulator by Aaron Giles and the MAME team (license: BSD-3-Clause)

options.label: 3dfx Voodoo Performance
options.desc:
Options to tweak the behavior of the 3dfx Voodoo emulation.
Switching to OpenGL requires a restart.
If OpenGL is available, host-side 3D acceleration is used which can make 3D rendering much faster.
Auto will use OpenGL if it is the active video driver in the frontend.

options.label: 3dfx Voodoo OpenGL Scaling
options.desc: Increase the native resolution of the rendered image.

options.label: 3dfx Voodoo Gamma Correction
options.desc: Change brightness of rendered 3dfx output.

options.label: Aspect Ratio Correction
options.desc: Adjust the aspect ratio to approximate what a CRT monitor would display (works best on high resolution displays and without integer scaling).

options.label: Overscan Border Size
options.desc: When enabled, show a border around the display. Some games use the color of the border to convey information.

options.label: Memory Size (restart required)
options.desc:
The amount of (high) memory that the emulated machine has. You can also disable extended memory (EMS/XMS).
Using more than the default is not recommended, due to incompatibility with certain games and applications.

options.label: Modem Type
options.desc: Type of emulated modem on COM1 for netplay. With the dial-up modem, one side needs to dial any number to connect.

options.label: CPU Type (restart required)

values.label: Auto - Mixed feature set with maximum performance and compatibility
386 (slow) - 386 instruction set with memory privilege checks
386 (prefetch) - With prefetch queue emulation (only on 'auto' and 'normal' core)
486 (slow) - 486 instruction set with memory privilege checks
Pentium (slow) - 586 instruction set with memory privilege checks

options.desc:
Emulated CPU type. Auto is the fastest choice.
Games that require specific CPU type selection:
386 (prefetch): X-Men: Madness in The Murderworld, Terminator 1, Contra, Fifa International Soccer 1994
486 (slow): Betrayal in Antara
Pentium (slow): Fifa International Soccer 1994, Windows 95/Windows 3.x games

options.label: Advanced > CPU Core

values.label: Auto - Real-mode games use normal, protected-mode games use dynamic
Dynamic - Dynamic recompilation (fast, using dynamic_x86 implementation)
Simple (interpreter optimized for old real-mode games)

options.desc: Emulation method (DOSBox CPU core) used.

options.label: Advanced > OS Disk Modifications (restart required)
options.desc:
When running an installed operating system, modifications to the C: drive will be made on the disk image by default.
Setting it to 'Discard' allows the content to be closed any time without worry of file system or registry corruption.
When using 'Save Difference Per Content' the disk image must never be modified again, otherwise existing differences become unusable.

options.label: Advanced > Free Space on D: in OS (restart required)

values.label: Disable D: Hard Disk (use only CD-ROM)

options.desc:
Controls the amount of free space available on the D: drive when running an installed operating system.
If the total size of the D: drive (data + free space) exceeds 2 GB, it can't be used in earlier versions of Windows 95.
WARNING: Created save files are tied to this setting, so changing this will hide all existing D: drive changes.

options.label: Advanced > Force Normal Core in OS
options.desc:
The normal core can be more stable when running an installed operating system.
This can be toggled on and off to navigate around crashes.

options.label: Audio Sample Rate (restart required)
options.desc: This should match the frontend audio output rate (Hz) setting.

options.label: SoundBlaster Settings
options.desc: Set the address, interrupt, low 8-bit and high 16-bit DMA.

options.label: MIDI Output
options.desc:
Select the .SF2 SoundFont file, .ROM file or interface used for MIDI output.
To add SoundFonts or ROM files, copy them into the 'system' directory of the frontend.
To use the frontend MIDI driver, make sure it's set up correctly.

options.label: Advanced > SoundBlaster Type
options.desc: Type of emulated SoundBlaster card.

options.label: Advanced > SoundBlaster Adlib/FM Mode

values.label: Auto (select based on the SoundBlaster type) (default)
Dual OPL-2 (Dual OPL-2 used by SoundBlaster Pro 1.0 for stereo sound)
OPL-3 Gold (AdLib Gold / OPL-3 / Yamaha YMF262)

options.desc: The SoundBlaster emulated FM synth mode. All modes are Adlib compatible except CMS.

options.label: Advanced > SoundBlaster Adlib Provider
options.desc: Provider for the Adlib emulation. Default has good quality and low performance requirements.

options.label: Advanced > Enable Gravis Ultrasound (restart required)
options.desc:
Enable Gravis Ultrasound emulation. Settings are fixed at port 0x240, IRQ 5, DMA 3.
If the ULTRADIR variable needs to be different than the default 'C:\ULTRASND' you need to issue 'SET ULTRADIR=...' in the command line or in a batch file.

options.label: Advanced > Enable Tandy Sound Device (restart required)
options.desc: Enable Tandy Sound Device emulation even when running without Tandy Graphics Adapter emulation.

options.label: Advanced > Swap Stereo Channels
options.desc: Swap the left and the right audio channel.

options.label: Use 32-bits color depth when available
options.desc: Render in 32-bit color when the game supports it for smoother gradients; disable to force 16-bit and save a little memory/bandwidth.

options.label: Vertical mode
options.desc: Rotates output for vertical (TATE) arcade games so upright screens display correctly on a normal monitor.

options.label: Force 60Hz
options.desc: Forces a 60Hz refresh regardless of the game's native rate, avoiding host-sync stutter at the cost of slightly off timing.

options.label: Resolution
options.desc: Output resolution for games that render at a variable size (e.g. some 3D/vector titles); higher is sharper but costs more.

options.label: Fixed Frameskip

values.label: Skip rendering of 1 frames out of 2
Skip rendering of 2 frames out of 3
Skip rendering of 3 frames out of 4
Skip rendering of 4 frames out of 5
Skip rendering of 5 frames out of 6

options.desc: Always skips a fixed number of rendered frames to save CPU/GPU; higher values are choppier but faster.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: How frames are skipped to keep speed: off, a fixed ratio, automatic on slowdown, or manual by threshold.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: With Manual frameskip, the audio-buffer occupancy percent below which a frame is dropped to keep sound from stuttering.

options.label: CPU clock
options.desc: Over/underclocks the emulated CPU; above 100% reduces in-game slowdown, below 100% slows the game down.

options.label: Diagnostic Input
options.desc: Button combo used to open the arcade board's service/test menu for diagnostics and settings.

options.label: Hiscores
options.desc: Saves and reloads arcade high-score tables between sessions using the hiscore.dat database.

options.label: Allow patched romsets
options.desc: Permits loading fan-patched or modified romsets instead of rejecting them as non-standard.

options.label: Samplerate
options.desc: Audio output sample rate in Hz; 48000 matches most hosts, 44100 can reduce load slightly.

options.label: Sample Interpolation
options.desc: Interpolation quality for sampled (PCM) audio; higher order sounds smoother but costs a little more CPU.

options.label: FM Interpolation
options.desc: Interpolation for FM sound-chip audio; enabling 4-point 3rd order gives cleaner FM tones.

options.label: LowPass Filter
options.desc: Applies a low-pass filter to soften harsh high frequencies for a mellower, more authentic speaker sound.

options.label: Analog Speed
options.desc: Sensitivity/speed of emulated analog controls (e.g. dials, paddles) as a percentage of normal.

options.label: SOCD Setting
options.desc: How simultaneous opposite cardinal directions (e.g. Left+Right) are resolved for fight-stick/keyboard input.

options.label: Crosshair emulation
options.desc: Controls when the on-screen aiming crosshair is shown for lightgun games.

options.label: Neo-Geo mode

values.label: Use bios set in BIOS dipswitch

options.desc: Selects the Neo-Geo BIOS/region (MVS arcade, AES home, or UniBIOS) affecting language, region and features.

options.label: Memory card mode
options.desc: Neo-Geo memory card behavior for saving progress: off, one shared card, or a separate card per game.

options.label: Debug Dip 1_1
options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 1, bit 1; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 1, bit 2; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 2, bit 5; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 2, bit 6; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.label: Debug Dip 2_7
options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 2, bit 7; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.label: Debug Dip 2_8
options.desc: Developer debug DIP switch bank 2, bit 8; leave off unless testing specific board behavior.

options.label: DIP Switch (per-game, dynamically generated)
options.desc: Per-game hardware DIP switch settings (difficulty, lives, region, etc.), generated dynamically for the loaded title.

options.label: Cheat (per-game, dynamically generated)
options.desc: Per-game cheat toggles loaded from the cheat database for the current title.

options.label: IPS Patch (per-game, dynamically generated)
options.desc: Per-game IPS patch options (translations, hacks, fixes) available for the loaded romset.

options.label: Romdata selection (per-game, dynamically generated)
options.desc: Per-game romdata variant selection for titles that offer alternate rom configurations.

options.label: PGM2 IC Card slot (per-game, dynamically generated)
options.desc: Per-game PGM2 IC-card slot selection used by IGS PGM2 arcade titles.

options.label: Region
options.desc: Sets the emulated Dreamcast's region (Japan/USA/Europe), affecting BIOS behavior and region-locked games.

options.label: Language
options.desc: Changes the language used by the BIOS and by any games that contain multiple languages.

options.label: HLE BIOS (Restart Required)
options.desc: Force use of high-level emulation BIOS.

options.label: Enable DSP
options.desc: Enable emulation of the Dreamcast's audio DSP (digital signal processor). Improves the accuracy of generated sound, but increases performance requirements.

options.label: Allow Arcade Service Buttons
options.desc: Enables SERVICE button for arcade games, to enter cabinet settings.

options.label: Set NAOMI Games to Free Play
options.desc: Modify to coin settings of the game to free play.

options.label: Coin Limit
options.desc: Disable coin insertion after defined limit.

options.label: Broadband Adapter Emulation
options.desc: Emulate the Ethernet broadband adapter instead of the modem. (Restart Required)

options.label: Enable UPnP
options.desc: Use UPnP to automatically configure your Internet router for online games.

options.label: Use DCNet
options.desc: Use the DCNet cloud service for Dreamcast Internet access.

options.label: Internal Resolution
options.desc: Modify rendering resolution.

options.label: Cable Type
options.desc: The output signal type. 'TV (Composite)' is the most widely supported.

options.label: Broadcast Standard
options.desc: TV broadcast standard (NTSC/PAL variants) for the emulated console, affecting refresh rate and video timing.

options.label: Screen Orientation
options.desc: Rotates the display to horizontal or vertical, for TATE (vertical-monitor) NAOMI/arcade titles.

options.label: Alpha Sorting
options.desc: Select how the transparent polygons are sorted.

options.label: Alpha Sort Key (MovieTheater)
options.desc: Which depth value keys each triangle in per-triangle alpha sorting. 'min' is stock flycast. The 'tie' variants collapse near-equal depths so co-planar decals keep their submitted order.

options.label: Accumulation Pixel Buffer Size
options.desc: Higher values might be required for higher resolutions to output correctly.

options.label: Maximum Transparent Layers
options.desc: Higher values might be required for complex scenes.

options.label: Full framebuffer emulation
options.desc: Enable full framebuffer emulation in VRAM. This is useful for games that directly read or write the framebuffer in VRAM. When enabled, Internal Resolution is forced to 640x480 and performance may be severely impacted.

options.label: Enable RTT (Render To Texture) Buffer
options.desc: Copy rendered textures back from the GPU to VRAM. This option is normally enabled for games that require it. When enabled, texture rendering upscaling is disabled and performance may be impacted.

options.label: Mipmapping
options.desc: When enabled textures will use smaller version of themselves when they appear farther away, it can increase performances and reduce shimmering.

options.label: Fog Effects
options.desc: Enables Dreamcast fog effects; disable only if fog causes visual glitches.

options.label: Volume Modifier
options.desc: A Dreamcast GPU feature that is typically used by games to draw object shadows. This should normally be enabled - the performance impact is usually minimal to negligible.

options.label: Anisotropic Filtering
options.desc: Enhance the quality of textures on surfaces that are at oblique viewing angles with respect to the camera. Higher values are more demanding on the GPU. Changes to this setting only apply after restarting.

options.label: Texture Filtering
options.desc: The texture filtering mode to use. This can be used to force a certain texture filtering mode on all textures to get a crisper (or smoother) appearance than Default. Values other than Default may cause various rendering issues. Changes to this setting only apply after restarting.

options.label: Delay Frame Swapping
options.desc: Useful to avoid flashing screens or glitchy videos. Not recommended on slow platforms.

options.label: Detect Frame Rate Changes
options.desc: Notify frontend when internal frame rate changes (e.g. from 60 fps to 30 fps). Improves frame pacing in games that run at a locked 30 fps or 20 fps, but should be disabled for games with unlocked (unstable) frame rates (e.g. Ecco the Dolphin, Unreal Tournament). Note: Unavailable when 'Auto Skip Frame' is enabled.

options.label: PowerVR2 Post-processing Filter
options.desc: Post-process the rendered image to simulate effects specific to the PowerVR2 GPU and analog video signals.

options.label: Texture Upscaling (xBRZ)
options.desc: Enhance hand-drawn 2D pixel art graphics. Should only be used with 2D pixelated games.

options.label: Texture Upscaling Max. Filtered Size
options.desc: Select a maximum size value for a texture to be upscaled, if the texture size is higher than the selected value then it will not be upscaled.

options.label: Native Depth Interpolation
options.desc: Helps with texture corruption and depth issues on AMD GPUs. Can also help Intel GPUs in some cases.

options.label: Fix Upscale Bleeding Edge
options.desc: Helps with texture bleeding case when upscaling. Disabling it can help if pixels are warping when upscaling in 2D games (MVC2, CVS, KOF, etc.)

options.label: Threaded Rendering
options.desc: Runs the GPU and CPU on different threads. Highly recommended.

options.label: Auto Skip Frame
options.desc: Automatically skip frames when the emulator is running slow. Note: This setting only applies when 'Threaded Rendering' is enabled.

options.label: Frame Skipping
options.desc: Sets the number of frames to skip between each displayed frame.

options.label: Widescreen Cheats (Restart Required)
options.desc: Activates cheats that allow certain games to display in widescreen format.

options.label: Widescreen Hack
options.desc: Draw geometry outside of the normal 4:3 aspect ratio. May produce graphical glitches in the revealed areas.

options.label: GD-ROM Fast Loading (inaccurate)
options.desc: Speeds up GD-ROM loading.

options.label: Dreamcast 32MB RAM Mod
options.desc: Enables 32MB RAM Mod for Dreamcast. May affect compatibility

options.label: SH4 CPU under/overclock
options.desc: Change the SH4 main CPU clock from the default 200 MHz. Underclocking may help slow platforms. Overclocking may increase the frame rate for some games. Use with caution.

options.label: Load Custom Textures
options.desc: Load custom textures located in the 'system/dc/textures/<game-id>/' folder.

options.label: Preload Custom Textures
options.desc: Preload custom textures at game start. May improve performance but increases memory usage.

options.label: Dump Textures
options.desc: Every time a new texture is used by the game, it will be saved as a .png file in the 'system/dc/texdump/<game-id>/' folder.

options.label: Dump Replaced Textures
options.desc: Always dump textures that are already replaced by custom textures.

options.label: Analog Stick Deadzone
options.desc: Select how far you have to push the analog stick before it starts being processed.

options.label: Trigger Deadzone
options.desc: Select how much you have to press the trigger before it starts being processed.

options.label: Digital Triggers
options.desc: When enabled the triggers will act as regular buttons, meaning they will be processed as either fully pressed or not pressed at all, with no in-between.

options.label: Broadcast Digital Outputs
options.desc: Broadcast digital outputs and force-feedback state on TCP port 8000. Compatible with the "-output network" MAME option.

options.label: Show Light Gun Settings
options.desc: Enable configuration of light gun crosshair display options. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Gun Crosshair Size Scaling
options.desc: Scales the on-screen light-gun crosshair from 50% to 300% of its base size.

options.label: Gun Crosshair 1 Display
options.desc: Shows and colors the player 1 light-gun crosshair, or hides it when disabled.

options.label: Gun Crosshair 2 Display
options.desc: Shows and colors the player 2 light-gun crosshair, or hides it when disabled.

options.label: Gun Crosshair 3 Display
options.desc: Shows and colors the player 3 light-gun crosshair, or hides it when disabled.

options.label: Gun Crosshair 4 Display
options.desc: Shows and colors the player 4 light-gun crosshair, or hides it when disabled.

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot A1
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot A1 (port A slot 1).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot A2
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot A2 (port A slot 2).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot B1
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot B1 (port B slot 1).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot B2
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot B2 (port B slot 2).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot C1
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot C1 (port C slot 1).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot C2
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot C2 (port C slot 2).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot D1
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot D1 (port D slot 1).

options.label: Device in Expansion Slot D2
options.desc: Select the device plugged in the expansion slot D2 (port D slot 2).

options.label: Per-Game Visual Memory Units/Systems (VMU)
options.desc:
When disabled, all games share up to 8 VMU save files (A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2) located in RetroArch's system folder.
The 'VMU A1' setting creates a unique VMU 'A1' file in RetroArch's save folder for each game that is launched.
The 'All VMUs' setting creates up to 8 unique VMU files (A1/A2/B1/B2/C1/C2/D1/D2) for each game that is launched.

options.label: Visual Memory Units/Systems (VMU) Sounds
options.desc: When enabled, VMU beeps are played.

options.label: DreamPotato VMU storage
options.desc: Enable storage of VMU data on the connected DreamPotato emulator. When enabled, the local VMU save file is not used.

options.label: Show Visual Memory Unit/System (VMU) Display Settings
options.desc: Enable configuration of emulated VMU LCD screen visibility, size, position and color. NOTE: Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Display
options.desc: Overlays the player 1 VMU (memory card) LCD screen on the game display.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Position
options.desc: Sets which screen corner the player 1 VMU overlay appears in.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Size
options.desc: Scales the player 1 VMU overlay from 1x to 5x its base size.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Pixel On Color
options.desc: Color used for lit (on) pixels of the player 1 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Pixel Off Color
options.desc: Color used for unlit (off) pixels of the player 1 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 1 Opacity
options.desc: Transparency of the player 1 VMU overlay, from 10% to fully opaque.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Display
options.desc: Overlays the player 2 VMU (memory card) LCD screen on the game display.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Position
options.desc: Sets which screen corner the player 2 VMU overlay appears in.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Size
options.desc: Scales the player 2 VMU overlay from 1x to 5x its base size.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Pixel On Color
options.desc: Color used for lit (on) pixels of the player 2 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Pixel Off Color
options.desc: Color used for unlit (off) pixels of the player 2 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 2 Opacity
options.desc: Transparency of the player 2 VMU overlay, from 10% to fully opaque.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Display
options.desc: Overlays the player 3 VMU (memory card) LCD screen on the game display.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Position
options.desc: Sets which screen corner the player 3 VMU overlay appears in.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Size
options.desc: Scales the player 3 VMU overlay from 1x to 5x its base size.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Pixel On Color
options.desc: Color used for lit (on) pixels of the player 3 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Pixel Off Color
options.desc: Color used for unlit (off) pixels of the player 3 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 3 Opacity
options.desc: Transparency of the player 3 VMU overlay, from 10% to fully opaque.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Display
options.desc: Overlays the player 4 VMU (memory card) LCD screen on the game display.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Position
options.desc: Sets which screen corner the player 4 VMU overlay appears in.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Size
options.desc: Scales the player 4 VMU overlay from 1x to 5x its base size.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Pixel On Color
options.desc: Color used for lit (on) pixels of the player 4 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Pixel Off Color
options.desc: Color used for unlit (off) pixels of the player 4 VMU overlay screen.

options.label: VMU Screen 4 Opacity
options.desc: Transparency of the player 4 VMU overlay, from 10% to fully opaque.

options.label: Default Player 1 Controller (Restart)
options.desc: Specify whether the Left or Right Controller is set to Player 1 as the default.

options.label: Onscreen Interactive Keypad Overlays (Restart and Touchscreen/Mouse Required)
options.desc: Enable multi-screen mode with onscreen interactive keypad overlays (370x600 PNG files) and side-by-side game/keypad display. Changing this setting requires a core restart. Mouse or touchscreen input is required to interact with the keypad overlays.

options.label: Refresh Rate (restart)
options.desc: Select which refresh rate will be used in emulation. 'Auto' automatically selects the best refresh rate based on the loaded content. 'NTSC (60 Hz)' forces 60 Hz. 'PAL (50 Hz)' forces 50 Hz.

options.label: Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Select which aspect ratio will be presented by the core. '1:1 PAR' selects an aspect ratio that produces square pixels.

options.label: Overscan
options.desc: Select which overscan (borders) will be used in emulation. 'Disabled' shows no overscan. 'Top+Bottom' enables vertical overscan only. 'Full (284 width)' and 'Full (320 width)' enable full overscan with different horizontal widths.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.desc: Remove the per-line sprite limit. This reduces flickering but may cause glitches in certain games. It's best to keep this option disabled.

options.label: Allow Up+Down / Left+Right
options.desc: Allow pressing, quickly alternating, or holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement based glitches in certain games.

options.label: Spinner Support
options.desc: Select which spinner controller will be emulated. Spinners are controlled by mouse movement. Mouse buttons are mapped to Left (Yellow) and Right (Red) buttons.

options.label: Spinner Sensitivity
options.desc: Set the sensitivity of the spinner controller. 1 is the lowest sensitivity and 10 is the highest.

options.label: System Hardware
options.desc: Runs loaded content with a specific emulated console. 'Auto' will select the most appropriate system for the current game.

options.label: System Region
options.desc: Specify which region the system is from. For consoles other than the Game Gear, 'PAL' is 50 Hz, while 'NTSC' is 60 Hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Force VDP Mode
options.desc: Overrides the VDP mode to force it to run at either NTSC 60Hz or PAL 50Hz, regardless of system region.

options.label: System Boot ROM
options.desc: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory. Displays console-specific start-up sequence/animation, then runs loaded content.

options.label: CD System BRAM (Requires Restart)
options.desc: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single save file between all games from a specific region (Per-BIOS) or to create a separate save file for each game (Per-Game). Note that the Sega CD/Mega-CD has limited internal storage, sufficient only for a handful of titles. To avoid running out of space, the 'Per-Game' setting is recommended.

options.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM (Requires Restart)
options.desc: When running Sega CD/Mega-CD content, specifies whether to share a single backup ram cart for all games (Per-Cart) or to create a separate backup ram cart for each game (Per-Game).

options.label: CD Backup Cart BRAM Size (Requires Restart)
options.desc: Sets the backup ram cart size when running Sega CD/Mega-CD content. Useful when setting the backup ram cart to Per-Game to avoid multiple larger cart sizes.

options.label: CD add-on (MD mode) (Requires Restart)
options.desc: Specify which add-on to use for CD audio playback with supported Mega Drive/Genesis games.

options.label: Cartridge Lock-On
options.desc: Lock-On Technology is a Mega Drive/Genesis feature that allowed an older game to connect to the pass-through port of a special cartridge for extended or altered gameplay. This option specifies which type of special 'lock-on' cartridge to emulate. A corresponding bios file must be present in RetroArch's system directory.

options.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: Borders
options.desc: Enable this to display the overscan regions at the top/bottom and/or left/right of the screen. These would normally be hidden by the bezel around the edge of a standard-definition television.

options.label: Hide Master System Side Borders
options.desc: Cuts off 8 pixels from either the left side of the screen, or both left and right sides when running Master System games.

options.label: Game Gear Extended Screen
options.desc: Forces Game Gear titles to run in SMS mode, with an increased resolution of 256x192. May show additional content, but typically displays a border of corrupt/unwanted image data.

options.label: Blargg NTSC Filter
options.desc: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

options.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
options.desc: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and Genesis Nomad LCD panels.

options.label: Interlaced Mode 2 Output
options.desc: Interlaced Mode 2 allows the Mega Drive/Genesis to output a double height (high resolution) 320x448 image by drawing alternate scan lines each frame (this is used by Sonic the Hedgehog 2 and Combat Cars multiplayer modes). 'Double Field' mimics original hardware, producing a sharp image with flickering/interlacing artifacts. 'Single Field' applies a deinterlacing filter, which stabilizes the image but causes mild blurring.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Master System FM (YM2413)
options.desc: Enable emulation of the FM Sound Unit used by certain Sega Mark III/Master System games for enhanced audio output.

options.label: Master System FM (YM2413) Core
options.desc: Select method used to emulate the FM Sound Unit of the Sega Mark III/Master System. 'MAME' option is fast, and runs full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' option is cycle accurate, very high quality, and has substantial CPU requirements.

options.label: Mega Drive/Genesis FM
options.desc: Select method used to emulate the FM synthesizer (main sound generator) of the Mega Drive/Genesis. 'MAME' options are fast, and run full speed on most systems. 'Nuked' options are cycle accurate, very high quality, and have substantial CPU requirements. The YM2612 chip is used by the original Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. The YM3438 is used in later Mega Drive/Genesis revisions.

options.label: Sound Output
options.desc: Select stereo or mono sound playback.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis.

options.label: Low-Pass Filter %
options.desc: Specify the cut-off frequency of the audio low pass filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: PSG Preamp Level
options.desc: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated SN76496 4-channel Programmable Sound Generator found in the SG-1000, Sega Mark III, Master System, Game Gear and Mega Drive/Genesis.

options.label: FM Preamp Level
options.desc: Set the audio preamplifier level of the emulated Mega Drive/Genesis FM sound synthesizer or Sega Mark III/Master System FM Sound Unit.

options.label: CD-DA Volume
options.desc: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated CD audio playback output.

options.label: PCM Volume
options.desc: Adjust the mixing volume of the emulated Sega CD/Mega-CD RF5C164 PCM sound generator output.

options.label: EQ Low
options.desc: Adjust the low range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: EQ Mid
options.desc: Adjust the middle range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: EQ High
options.desc: Adjust the high range band of the internal audio equalizer.

options.label: Light Gun Input
options.desc: Use a mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input.

options.label: Show Light Gun Crosshair
options.desc: Display light gun crosshairs when using the MD Menacer, MD Justifiers and MS Light Phaser input device types.

options.label: Invert Mouse Y-Axis
options.desc: Inverts the Y-axis of the MD Mouse input device type.

options.label: Remove Per-Line Sprite Limit
options.desc: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

options.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll
options.desc: Allows each individual cell to be scrolled vertically, instead of 16px 2-cell, by averaging out with the vscroll value of the neighbouring cell. This hack only applies to few games that use 2-cell vertical scroll mode.

options.label: Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll limit
options.desc: Only when Enhanced per-tile vertical scroll is enabled. Adjusts the limit of the vertical scroll enhancement. When the vscroll difference between neighbouring tiles is bigger than this limit, the enhancement is disabled.

options.label: CPU Speed
options.desc: Overclock the emulated CPU. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.

options.label: System Lock-Ups
options.desc: Emulate system lock-ups that occur on real hardware when performing illegal address access. This should only be disabled when playing certain demos and homebrew that rely on illegal behavior for correct operation.

options.label: 68K Address Error
options.desc: The Mega Drive/Genesis main CPU (Motorola 68000) generates an Address Error exception (crash) when attempting to perform unaligned memory access. Enabling this will simulate this behavior. It should only be disabled when playing ROM hacks, since these are typically developed using less accurate emulators and may rely on invalid RAM access for correct operation.

options.label: CD Access Time
options.desc: Simulate original CD hardware latency when initiating a read or seeking to a specific location on loaded disc. This is required by a few CD games that crash if CD data is available too soon and also fixes CD audio desync issues in some games. Disabling this can be useful with MSU-MD games as it makes CD audio tracks loops more seamless.

options.label: CD Image Cache
options.desc: Load CD image to memory on startup. CHD supported only. Restart Required.

options.label: Show Advanced Audio Volume Settings (Reopen menu)
options.desc: Enable configuration of low-level audio channel parameters. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.desc: Reduce the volume of the Mega Drive/Genesis FM Channel 2. Only works with MAME FM emulators.

options.label: Resolution

options.label: ST-V Service/Test Buttons
options.desc: Enable Service/Test for ST-V, to enter cabinet settings.

options.label: ST-V Favorite Region
options.desc: Choose favorite bios region for STV.

options.label: Bios Language
options.desc: Choose your favorite language, will translate some games. Requires a restart.

options.label: Auto-rotate Screen
options.desc: Virtually rotate screen orientation and button mappings automatically for known games. When set to 'Manual', screen rotation is adjusted by pressing the SELECT button, otherwise a fixed rotation can be set to either 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees counter-clockwise.

options.label: Force 60Hz
options.desc: Force 60Hz instead of original 75Hz refresh rate, for perfectly smooth movement on 60Hz displays

options.label: Language (*)
