(*) Core restart required.

options.label: Color Palette
options.desc: Composite tries to recreate the original console output and can show more details in some games.

options.label: Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: Resolution Scaling
options.desc: 'Auto' will allow the resolution to change. 'Low Resolution' can crush pixels. 'High Resolution' will stay on the maximum width.

options.label: High Resolution Blending Strength
options.desc: Blend pixels together when in High Resolution mode. Higher values will blur the picture more.

options.label: Show Horizontal Overscan
options.desc: 'Auto' will try to adapt to games, cropping empty areas.

options.label: Initial Scanline
options.desc: First rendered scanline. Higher values will crop the top of the image.

options.label: Last Scanline
options.desc: Last rendered scanline. Lower values will crop the bottom of the image.

options.label: PSG Audio Chip (Restart Required)
options.desc: HuC6280 represents the original PC Engine, HuC6280A the SuperGrafx and CoreGrafx I.

options.label: Owl Resampler Quality
options.desc: Higher values give better signal-to-noise ratio and preservation of higher frequencies but increase the computation cost and may cause higher latency and clipping if the volume is set too high.

options.label: Show Advanced Input/Turbo Settings
options.desc: Show Multitap, Mouse, Turbo Buttons and advanced parameters. NOTE: You may need to go back in game and re-enter the menu to refresh the list.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.desc: Higher values will make the mouse cursor move faster.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directions
options.desc: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: Disable Soft Reset (RUN+SELECT)
options.desc: When RUN and SELECT are pressed simultaneously, disable both buttons temporarily instead of resetting.

options.label: Multitap 5-port Controller
options.desc: Enable up to 5-player multitap emulation. Disabling this is only needed in some cases (e.g. Cho Aniki).

options.label: P1 Default Joypad Type
options.desc: Choose if port 1 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P2 Default Joypad Type
options.desc: Choose if port 2 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P3 Default Joypad Type
options.desc: Choose if port 3 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P4 Default Joypad Type
options.desc: Choose if port 4 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: P5 Default Joypad Type
options.desc: Choose if port 5 joypad should be 2 or 6 buttons by default. This option is only applied when the core starts, if you want to switch while content is running, use the 'Mode Switch' button. NOTE: 6 buttons joypad can have weird behaviors in non compatible games.

options.label: Turbo Hotkey Mode
options.desc: Enable turbo buttons. Hotkeys (buttons III and IV) can behave as either toggle switches or dedicated (hold to use) turbo buttons.

options.label: Alternate Turbo Hotkey
options.desc: Assign RetroPad's L3/R3 buttons as turbo hotkeys instead of buttons III and IV. Works only in 'Toggle' mode and only as long as nothing is assigned to the L3/R3 buttons. You can avoid remapping buttons III and IV when switching to 6-button controller mode with this.

options.label: Turbo Speed
options.desc: Choose how fast button presses are repeated.

options.label: CD Image Cache (Restart Required)
options.desc: Load the complete image into memory at startup. Can potentially decrease loading times at the cost of an increased startup time.

options.label: CD Bios (Restart Required)
options.desc: Most games can run on 'System Card 3'. 'Games Express' is needed for several unlicensed games.

options.label: Arcade Card (Restart Required)
options.desc: Leave this option enabled to allow enhanced modes of ACD-enhanced SCD games.

options.label: CD Speed
options.desc: Higher values enable faster loading times but can cause issues with a couple of games.

options.label: ADPCM precision
options.desc: Full precision of 12-bits for the MSM5205 ADPCM predictor can reduce whining noise during ADPCM playback.

options.label: ADPCM Volume %
options.desc: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: CDDA Volume %
options.desc: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: CD PSG Volume %
options.desc: CD game only. Setting this volume control too high may cause sample clipping.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.desc: Remove 16-sprites-per-scanline hardware limit. WARNING: May cause graphics glitching on some games (such as Bloody Wolf).

options.label: CPU Overclock Multiplier
options.desc: Higher values can reduce slowdowns in games. WARNING: Can cause glitches and crashes.

options.label: 3D mode
options.desc: Select the 3D mode. Anaglyph - used in conjunction with classic dual-lens-color glasses. Cyberscope - intended for use with the CyberScope 3D device. sidebyside - the left-eye image is displayed on the left, and the right-eye image is displayed on the right. vli - Vertical lines alternate between left and right view. hli - Horizontal lines alternate between left and right view.

options.label: Anaglyph preset
options.desc: Anaglyph preset colors.

options.label: Side-by-side separation
options.desc: Number of pixels to separate left and right views in side-by-side 3D mode.

options.label: Allow Opposite Directions
options.desc: Allow pressing up and down or left and right directions at the same time. This may cause glitches.

options.label: CPU emulation  (Restart)
options.desc: Choose between faster and accurate (slower) emulation.

options.label: Display Rotation
options.desc: Choose the orientation of the console screen. 'Portrait' can be used to achieve the correct layout of portrait oriented games on a conventional (landscape) display. 'Manual' enables rotation via the controller (default button: SELECT).

options.label: Rotate Button Mappings
options.desc: Choose the preferred button mapping. 'Auto' adjusts button mapping to match the current display rotation.

options.label: Color Palette
options.desc: Choose the colorization of WonderSwan (Mono) games. 'WS' palettes mimic the display of the original WonderSwan hardware.

options.label: Color Depth (Restart Required)
options.desc: 24-bit is slower and not available on all platforms.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilizes the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', this specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: 60Hz Mode
options.desc: Update the display at 60Hz instead of the native 75Hz WonderSwan refresh rate by dropping every fifth frame. Reduces video smoothness, but avoids screen tearing on displays that do not support native operation above 60Hz.

options.label: Sound Output Sample Rate
options.desc: Higher values improve sound quality slightly at the expense of performance.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Apply a low pass audio filter to 'soften' the sometimes harsh chiptunes produced by the WonderSwan.

options.label: Boot Game Directly
options.desc: Choose if the core should boot the game directly or if it should boot to the DS menu instead (BIOS and firmware files required).

options.label: Use Firmware Settings
options.desc: Use language and username from the DS firmware. When disabled or if firmware file was not found, the username will be provided by the Libretro frontend, if it's empty it will default to 'melonDS'.

options.label: Language
options.desc: Selected language will be used if 'Use Firmware Settings' is disabled or if firmware file was not found.

options.label: Microphone Input
options.desc: Choose the type of noise that will be used as microphone input.

options.label: Touch Mode
options.desc: Choose mode for interactions with the touch screen.

options.label: Swap Screen Mode
options.desc: Choose if the 'Swap screens' button should work on press or on hold.

options.label: Screen Layout
options.desc: Choose how many screens should be displayed and how they should be displayed.

options.label: Screen Gap
options.desc: Choose how large the gap between the 2 screens should be.

options.label: Hybrid Small Screen Mode
options.desc: Choose the position of the small screen when using a 'hybrid' mode, or if it should show both screens.

options.label: Game Boy Model (Restart)
options.desc: Runs loaded content with a specific Game Boy model. 'Autodetect' will select the most appropriate model for the current game.

options.label: Use BIOS File if Found (Restart)
options.desc: Use official BIOS/bootloader for emulated hardware, if present in RetroArch's system directory.

options.label: Skip BIOS Intro (Restart)
options.desc: When using an official BIOS/bootloader, skip the start-up logo animation. This setting is ignored when 'Use BIOS File if Found' is disabled.

options.label: Default Game Boy Palette
options.desc: Selects which palette is used for Game Boy games that are not Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy compatible, or if the model is forced to Game Boy.

options.label: Hardware Preset Game Boy Palettes (Restart)
options.desc: Use the palettes for Game Boy games that have presets on the Game Boy Color or Super Game Boy.

options.label: Use Super Game Boy Borders (Restart)
options.desc: Display Super Game Boy borders when running Super Game Boy enhanced games.

options.label: Color Correction
options.desc: Adjusts output colors to match the display of real GBA/GBC hardware.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.desc: Simulates LCD ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Smart' attempts to detect screen flickering, and only performs a 50:50 mix on affected pixels. 'LCD Ghosting' mimics natural LCD response times by combining multiple buffered frames. 'Simple' or 'Smart' blending is required when playing games that aggressively exploit LCD ghosting for transparency effects (Wave Race, Chikyuu Kaihou Gun ZAS, F-Zero, the Boktai series...).

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Enables a low pass audio filter to reduce the 'harshness' of generated audio.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.desc: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directional Input
options.desc: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: Solar Sensor Level
options.desc: Sets ambient sunlight intensity. Can be used by games that included a solar sensor in their cartridges, e.g: the Boktai series.

options.label: Game Boy Player Rumble (Restart)
options.desc: Enabling this will allow compatible games with the Game Boy Player boot logo to make the controller rumble. Due to how Nintendo decided this feature should work, it may cause glitches such as flickering or lag in some of these games.

options.label: Idle Loop Removal
options.desc: Reduce system load by optimizing so-called 'idle-loops' - sections in the code where nothing happens, but the CPU runs at full speed (like a car revving in neutral). Improves performance, and should be enabled on low-end hardware.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Frameskip Interval
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Fixed Interval', the value set here is the number of frames omitted after a frame is rendered - i.e. '0' = 60fps, '1' = 30fps, '2' = 15fps, etc.

options.label: RDP Plugin
options.desc: Select a RDP Plugin, use Angrylion (if available) for best compability, GLideN64 for Performance

options.label: 4:3 Resolution
options.desc: (GLN64) Select Render Viewport dimensions (4:3).

options.label: Wide Resolution
options.desc: (GLN64) Select Render Viewport dimensions for wider resolutions.

options.label: Aspect Ratio

options.label: Threaded Renderer

options.label: Hybrid Filter

options.label: Dithering

options.label: Dithering Quantization
options.desc: (GLN64) Dither with color quantization.

options.label: Image Dithering Mode
options.desc: (GLN64) Dithering mode for image in RDRAM.

options.label: MSAA level
options.desc: (GLN64) Anti-Aliasing level (0 = disabled).

options.label: FXAA
options.desc: (GLN64) Fast Approximate Anti-Aliasing shader, moderately blur textures (0 = disabled).

options.label: LOD Emulation
options.desc: (GLN64) Calculate per-pixel Level Of Details to select texture mip levels and blend them with each other using LOD fraction.

options.label: Framebuffer Emulation
options.desc: (GLN64) Frame/depth buffer emulation. Disabling it can shorten input lag for particular games, but also break some special effects.

options.label: Copy auxiliary buffers to RDRAM
options.desc: (GLN64) Copy auxiliary buffers to RDRAM (fixes some Game artifacts like Paper Mario Intro).

options.label: Color buffer to RDRAM

options.label: Enable color buffer copy from RDRAM
options.desc: (GLN64) Enable color buffer copy from RDRAM.

options.label: Depth buffer to RDRAM
options.desc: (GLN64) Depth buffer copy to RDRAM (Off will trade compatibility for Performance).

options.label: Background Mode
options.desc: (GLN64) Render backgrounds mode (HLE only). One piece (fast), Stripped (precise).

options.label: Hardware per-pixel lighting
options.desc: (GLN64) Standard per-vertex lighting when disabled. Slightly different rendering.

options.label: Continuous texrect coords
options.desc: (GLN64) Make texrect coordinates continuous to avoid black lines between them.

options.label: Enable inaccurate texture coordinates
options.desc: (GLN64) Enables inaccurate texture coordinate calculations. This can improve performance and texture pack compatibity at the cost of accuracy.

options.label: Enable native-res boundaries for texture coordinates
options.desc: (GLN64) Bound texture rectangle texture coordinates to the values they take in native resolutions. It prevents garbage due to fetching out of texture bounds, but can result in hard edges.

options.label: Native res. 2D texrects
options.desc: (GLN64) Render 2D texrects in native resolution to fix misalignment between parts of 2D image (example: Mario Kart driver selection portraits).

options.label: Less accurate blending mode
options.desc: (GLN64) Do not use shaders to emulate N64 blending modes. Works faster on slow GPU. Can cause glitches.

options.label: GPU shader depth write
options.desc: (GLN64) Enable writing of fragment depth. Some mobile GPUs do not support it, thus it's optional. Leave enabled.

options.label: N64 Depth Compare
options.desc: (GLN64) Enable N64 depth compare instead of OpenGL standard one. Experimental, Fast mode will have more glitches.

options.label: Cache GPU Shaders
options.desc: (GLN64) Use persistent storage for compiled shaders.

options.label: Cache Textures
options.desc: (GLN64) Save texture cache to hard disk.

options.label: Overscan

options.desc: (GLN64) Limit High-Res textures size in VRAM (in MB, 0 = no limit).

options.label: Max texture cache size
options.desc: (GLN64) Set Max texture cache size (in elements). Reduce it if you experience black textures leading to a crash.

options.label: Texture Enhancement
options.desc: (GLN64) Various Texture Filters ('As-Is' will just cache).

options.label: Don't filter background textures

options.desc: (GLN64) Enable High-Res Texture packs if available.

options.desc: (GLN64) Compress created texture caches.

options.desc: (GLN64) This should be enabled unless it's a old RICE Texture pack.

options.desc: (GLN64) Use in addition to Texture cache, will use lazy loading and trade memory consumption against loading speeds.

options.label: Use enhanced Hi-Res Storage
options.desc: (GLN64) Use in addition to High-Res textures, will use lazy loading and trade memory consumption against loading speeds.

options.label: INI Behaviour
options.desc: (GLN64) Specifies INI Settings behaviour. This should really only contain essential options. Changing this can and will break ROM's, if the correct options aren't set manually. Some options may only be set via INI (fbInfoDisabled).

options.label: (ParaLLEl-RDP) Synchronous RDP

options.label: (ParaLLEl-RDP) Crop overscan
options.desc: Crop pixels around edge of screen.

options.label: (ParaLLEl-RDP) VI Divot filter
options.desc: Allow VI divot filter, cleans up stray black pixels.

options.label: (ParaLLEl-RDP) VI Gamma dither

options.desc: Set the turbo pulse speed for the Turbo B and Turbo A buttons.

options.desc: Overclock the emulated CPU.

options.label: RAM Power-on State
options.desc: RAM values on power up. Some games rely on initial RAM values for random number generation as an example.

options.label: Emulated Hardware (Restart)
options.desc: Specify which console hardware to emulate. Requires the corresponding bios file to be present in the frontend 'system' directory (o2rom.bin, c52.bin, g7400.bin, jopac.bin).

options.label: Console Region (Restart)
options.desc: Specify which region the system is from. 'Auto' chooses the correct region based on emulated hardware. 'NTSC' is 60hz, 'PAL' is 50hz. Games may run abnormally if the wrong region is selected, and the setting my be overridden if the current content is incompatible.

options.label: Swap Gamepads
options.desc: Swap inputs from the two connected controllers of the emulated console. Required for games such as UFO and P.T. Barnum's Acrobats, which accept player 1 input from the second controller.

options.label: Virtual KBD Transparency
options.desc: Set transparency level of the virtual on-screen keyboard.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.desc: Remove the border around the edges of the screen, typically unused by games and hidden by the bezel of a standard-definition television.

options.label: Interframe Blending
options.desc: Simulate CRT phosphor ghosting effects. 'Simple' performs a 50:50 mix of the current and previous frames. 'Ghosting' accumulates pixels from multiple successive frames. May be used to alleviate screen flicker.

options.label: Audio Volume
options.desc: Set output audio volume level.

options.label: Voice Volume
options.desc: Set output volume level of 'The Voice' speech samples. The voice sampleset WAV files must be placed in the frontend 'system/voice' directory.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Apply a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound effects produced by most Odyssey2/Videopac+ games.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.desc: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: BIOS (rom1)
options.desc: Select system BIOS. Only ROMS present in the system directory are listed. Changes take affect at core start/restart.

options.label: Font (rom2)
options.desc: Select 'font rom'. Required by some Japanese games, otherwise optional. Only ROMs present in the system directory are listed. Changes take affect at core start/restart.

options.label: CPU Overclock
options.desc: Increase clock speed of the emulated 3DO's 12.5MHz ARM60 CPU. Dramatically improves frame rates in many games, but increases performance requirements and in some cases has no effect (or may cause glitches).

options.label: Memory Capacity
options.desc: Select the amount of DRAM and VRAM the system has. Only useful for homebrew and non-stock values may cause issues with some official software. Changes take affect at core start/restart. !EXPERIMENTAL!

options.label: CD Speed
options.desc: Select the effective CD-ROM read speed. Warning: can expose timing issues in some titles. Particularly above 16x.

options.label: Region / Mode
options.desc: Select the resolution and field rate. NOTE: some EU games require a EU ROM.

options.label: VDLP Pixel Format
options.desc: Select the pixel format to request from the runtime and convert to from the internal 16bpp format. Changes take affect at core start.

options.label: VDLP Bypass CLUT
options.desc: Force 3DO VDLP to bypass the game's CLUT (color lookup table). May result in incorrect colors but faster rendering.

options.label: HiRes CEL Rendering
options.desc: Enabling this option causes CELs to be rendered at 2x the resolution into a 2x output framebuffer, increasing the fidelity of 3D models. Will not affect 2D games. Has a significant performance impact.

options.label: MADAM Matrix Engine
options.desc: 'MADAM' is the 3DO's graphics accelerator. It contains a custom maths co-processor, used by the 3DO's CPU to offload matrix operations. This corresponds to running in 'Hardware' - but the 3DO could also utilise a built-in ARM 'Software' version of the MADAM matrix engine. 'Hardware' mode is the default, but it has been observed that some games run faster when forcing 'Software' mode. Changes take affect at core start/restart.

options.label: OperaOS SWI HLE
options.desc: 3DO games are built on top of Portfolio OS. Opera has high level emulation of certain OS functions. This HLE may improve performance in on certain games.

options.label: Threaded DSP
options.desc: Run the DSP (audio processor) on a separate CPU thread. Improves performance on multi-core systems. !EXPERIMENTAL!

options.label: NVRAM Storage
options.desc: Selects whether NVRAM saves should be created per-game or as a single NVRAM file shared between all games.

options.label: NVRAM Version
options.desc: Select the NVRAM version.

options.label: Active Input Devices
options.desc: Sets the maximum number of emulated input devices. Certain games, particularly when using >16x CDROM speed and have more than 1 emulated controller, causes content to ignore gamepad input or crash. Setting 'Active Input Devices' to 1 can be workaround for this issue on some titles.

options.label: Hide Lightgun Crosshairs
options.desc: Hides lightgun crosshairs for all players.

options.label: Debug Output
options.desc: Print 3DO debug port output to stderr. Only really useful to 3DO homebrew developers.

options.label: BIOS
options.desc: Selects which installed PS2 BIOS image to boot with; a valid BIOS is required to run games.

options.label: Fast Boot (Restart)
options.desc: Skips BIOS startup screen and boots straight to the game. Disable this if you want to access the PS2 system settings or access the Memory Card manager.

options.label: Fast CD/DVD Access (Restart)
options.desc: Fast CD/DVD access/seek times. A small handful of games will have compatibility problems with this enabled.

options.label: Shared Memory Cards (Restart)
options.desc: Use per-content or shared memory cards.

options.label: Enable Cheats
options.desc: Enable cheat files to be read from the 'cheats' directory in the system folder.

options.label: Language Unlock (Restart)
options.desc: If enabled, will look inside the internal database for language unlock options. Examples include: forcing an international Japanese version to English, unlocking more European languages, etc

options.label: Renderer
options.desc: Graphics backend used to render (Vulkan, D3D11/12, OpenGL, paraLLEl-GS, or software).

options.label: Internal Resolution (Restart)
options.desc: Internal render resolution as a multiple of native PS2 — higher is sharper but costs more GPU.

options.label: paraLLEl super sampling
options.desc: Apply supersampled anti-aliasing (SSAA). Unlike straight upscaling, supersampling retains a coherent visual look where 3D elements have similar resolution as UI elements. For high-res scanout upscaling to work, you need at least '4x SSAA ordered' (or higher). Setting this to 'Native' disables super sampling.

options.label: paraLLEl experimental High-res scanout
options.desc: Allows upscaling with paraLLEl. Doesn't work with every game, some might require patches on top. Requires Supersampling to be set to at least 4x SSAA ordered or higher for it to work.

options.label: paraLLEl experimental SSAA texture
options.desc: Feedback higher resolution textures. May help high-res scanout image quality. Highly experimental and may cause rendering glitches.

options.label: paraLLEl experimental sharp backbuffer
options.desc: Attempts to workaround games that add extra blit passes before scanning out. May lead to better image quality in certain games which do this.

options.label: Force Texture LOD0
options.desc: Disable this for traditional hardware mipmapping. Enabling this will bypass mipmapping and always use texture LOD0 instead. The result is better image quality. Only a small handful of games have graphics rendering issues with this enabled.

options.label: Deinterlacing
options.desc: Select a deinterlacing method. Use 'Automatic' if unsure what to pick.

options.label: Hardware Download Mode
options.desc: Controls how the GS reads rendered data back to the CPU (e.g. memory-card save images). 'Accurate' is the safest and matches hardware, but forces a CPU/GPU synchronization on every readback, which can sharply reduce the frame rate on screens that read back often (some save/load and stage-select menus) - this is especially severe with the paraLLEl-GS renderer. 'Unsynchronized' avoids that stall and is much faster, at the risk of incorrect results in the rare games that read back GPU-rendered content. 'Disable Readbacks' and 'Disabled' trade more accuracy for speed.

options.label: No interlacing hint (Restart)
options.desc: If enabled, will look in the internal database if a patch is available for the game to turn the image into either a non-interlaced, full frame, or progressive scan video signal, and/or a combination of all the above. Image will be more stable and Deinterlacing can be turned off.

options.label: Texture Filtering
options.desc: Texture smoothing mode (nearest, PS2-accurate, or forced bilinear) affecting image sharpness.

options.label: Trilinear Filtering
options.desc: Trilinear mipmap filtering mode to reduce shimmer on distant textures.

options.label: Anisotropic Filtering
options.desc: Sharpens textures viewed at steep angles; higher levels look better at a small GPU cost.

options.label: Dithering
options.desc: Dithering mode used to smooth color banding from the PS2's limited color depth.

options.label: Blending Accuracy
options.desc: How accurately GPU blending effects are emulated; higher fixes visual bugs but costs performance.

options.label: Widescreen hint (Restart)
options.desc: Applies a widescreen patch if a patch for the game can be found inside the internal database.

options.label: PCRTC Anti-Blur
options.desc: Disable this for the most accurate output image. Enabling this will attempt to deblur the image. Most noticeable on software renderer and paraLLEl.

options.label: PCRTC Screen Offsets
options.desc: Honors the PS2 CRTC screen offsets, correcting image positioning/shake in some games.

options.label: Disable Interlace Offset
options.desc: Disables the interlace field offset to reduce blur, at the cost of some vertical shimmer.

options.label: Auto Flush (Software)
options.desc: Auto-flushes the software renderer when textures overlap render targets, fixing some effects.

options.label: EE Cycle Rate
options.desc: Underclocks or overclocks the emulated Emotion Engine CPU to fix speed or slowdown issues.

options.label: EE Cycle Skipping
options.desc: Skips EE CPU cycles to boost speed on demanding games, risking glitches or audio problems.

options.label: Game Enhancements hint (Restart)
options.desc: Applies game-specific enhancements if patches for the game can be found inside the internal database. Examples of enhancements: LOD [Level of Detail] enhancements, better draw distance, ability to skip FMVs, etc.

options.label: Uncapped Framerate hint (Restart)
options.desc: Uncaps the framerate if a patch for the game can be found inside the internal database. This can turn a 30fps game into 60fps locked, or stabilize the framerate. You might have to increase EE Cycle Rate in combination with this for a stable locked framerate. 60fps PAL-to-NTSC does what it says if it can find a patch, otherwise it will just try to use the default uncapped framerate patch (50fps for PAL, 60fps for NTSC)

options.label: Deterministic FP (Soft-Float FPU+COP2) (Restart)
options.desc: Emulates the PS2's floating-point units bit-exactly in software (PS2Float) instead of using the host SSE units. Fixes a small number of games whose physics/AI depend on the PS2's non-IEEE rounding - Stuntman's recorded chase playback is the known case. Costs a lot of speed, so leave it off unless a game needs it. Applies to the EE FPU (COP1) and to VU0 (COP2 macro mode + VU0 micro programs); VU1 is untouched.

options.label: Deterministic FP: VU0 Micro Programs (Restart)
options.desc: Only applies when Deterministic FP is enabled. 'Interpreter' also runs VU0 micro programs (CALLMS) bit-exactly, which is the accurate choice but costs a lot. 'Recompiler' leaves them on microVU0 while COP2 macro mode stays bit-exact - much faster, and correct for games whose affected math is macro-mode only.

options.label: Deterministic FP Scope (Restart)
options.desc: Which operations the soft-float path covers when Deterministic FP is enabled. 'All' is the accurate choice; the narrower scopes trade accuracy for speed.

options.label: Enable Manual Hardware Renderer Fixes (Not Recommended)
options.desc: This will disable automatic settings from the database. Unless you know what you are doing it is NOT RECOMMENDED to turn this ON.

options.label: CPU Sprite Render Size
options.desc: Upscaling hack: renders large sprites on the CPU to fix upscaled texture artifacts.

options.label: CPU Sprite Render Level
options.desc: Chooses which primitive types the CPU sprite-render hack applies to.

options.label: Software CLUT Render
options.desc: Renders color-lookup-table textures in software to fix certain palette/graphical glitches.

options.label: GPU Target CLUT
options.desc: GPU CLUT-handling hack that fixes palette effects reading from render targets.

options.label: Auto Flush
options.desc: Flushes the GPU target when it's re-read as a texture, fixing self-referencing effects at a perf cost.

options.label: Texture Inside RT
options.desc: Handles textures sampled from inside a render target, fixing some post-processing effects.

options.label: Disabled Depth Conversion
options.desc: Skips depth-buffer conversions to save performance, at the risk of graphical errors.

options.label: Use External GameIndex Database
options.desc: Load the game-compatibility database from <system>/resources/GameIndex.yaml if present, falling back to the built-in database when it is missing. When disabled, always use the database built into the core.

options.label: Framebuffer Conversion
options.desc: Forces framebuffer format conversion on the CPU to fix specific rendering glitches.

options.label: Disable Partial Source Invalidation
options.desc: Disables partial texture-cache invalidation, a compatibility hack for some games.

options.label: GPU Palette Conversion
options.desc: Performs palette conversion on the GPU to reduce CPU load, fixing/altering some effects.

options.label: Preload Frame Data
options.desc: Preloads full frame texture data to fix missing graphics in some games at a performance cost.

options.label: Half Pixel Offset
options.desc: Corrects half-pixel alignment when upscaling to remove lines/gaps between sprites.

options.label: Native Scaling
options.desc: Renders certain passes at native resolution to reduce upscaling artifacts.

options.label: Round Sprite
options.desc: Rounds sprite coordinates when upscaling to fix vertical/horizontal seam lines.

options.label: Align Sprite
options.desc: Aligns sprites when upscaling to remove thin vertical lines between them.

options.label: Merge Sprite
options.desc: Merges adjacent sprites when upscaling to eliminate visible seams.

options.label: Unscaled Palette Texture Draws
options.desc: Draws palette textures unscaled to fix color/graphical errors when upscaling.

options.label: Force Even Sprite Position
options.desc: Forces even sprite positions when upscaling to remove misalignment artifacts.

options.label: Port 1 > Analog Deadzone
options.desc: Dead zone for Port 1 analog sticks; ignores small movements to prevent drift.

options.label: Port 1 > Trigger Deadzone
options.desc: Dead zone for Port 1 analog triggers before input registers.

options.label: Port 1 > Analog Sensitivity
options.desc: Analog stick sensitivity scaling for Port 1; higher amplifies stick movement.

options.label: Port 1 > Invert Left Analog Axis
options.desc: Inverts the Port 1 left analog stick axes (X, Y, or both).

options.label: Port 1 > Invert Right Analog Axis
options.desc: Inverts the Port 1 right analog stick axes (X, Y, or both).

options.label: Port 1 > Start in Analog Mode
options.desc: Start the controller in analog mode rather than digital. Some games (e.g. Ridge Racer V) boot the pad in digital and normally require pressing the controller's ANALOG button to enable the sticks; enable this to get analog controls from the start. Games that lock the controller mode are unaffected.

options.label: Port 1 > Rumble
options.desc: Enables and sets vibration strength for the Port 1 controller.

options.label: Port 2 > Analog Deadzone
options.desc: Dead zone for Port 2 analog sticks; ignores small movements to prevent drift.

options.label: Port 2 > Trigger Deadzone
options.desc: Dead zone for Port 2 analog triggers before input registers.

options.label: Port 2 > Analog Sensitivity
options.desc: Analog stick sensitivity scaling for Port 2; higher amplifies stick movement.

options.label: Port 2 > Invert Left Analog Axis
options.desc: Inverts the Port 2 left analog stick axes (X, Y, or both).

options.label: Port 2 > Invert Right Analog Axis
options.desc: Inverts the Port 2 right analog stick axes (X, Y, or both).

options.label: Port 2 > Start in Analog Mode
options.desc: Start the controller in analog mode rather than digital. Some games (e.g. Ridge Racer V) boot the pad in digital and normally require pressing the controller's ANALOG button to enable the sticks; enable this to get analog controls from the start. Games that lock the controller mode are unaffected.

options.label: Port 2 > Rumble
options.desc: Enables and sets vibration strength for the Port 2 controller.

options.label: Region
options.desc: Specify which region the system is from. 'NTSC' is 60 Hz while 'PAL' is 50 Hz. 'Auto' will detect the region of the currently loaded content. Games may run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: BIOS Selection
options.desc: Specify which BIOS to use. 'Auto' will attempt to load a real bios file from the frontend 'system' directory, falling back to high level emulation if unavailable. 'HLE' forces high level BIOS emulation. It is recommended to use an official bios file for better compatibility.

options.label: Show BIOS Name/Boot Logo
options.desc: When using a custom BIOS file, enables the display of its file name in the OSD. Also specifies whether to show the BIOS logo when starting or selecting Reset. Warning: Enabling the logo may reduce game compatibility.

options.label: Memory Card 1 Type (Restart)
options.desc: How to emulate the memory card in slot 1. 'Libretro' passes the card data to the frontend (usually saved as .srm). 'Game Code' saves it to a file named based on the serial, such as SCUS-00001_1.mcd, for compatibility with some other emulators.

options.label: Memory Card 2 Type
options.desc: Same as above, but card in slot 2.

options.label: CD read-ahead
options.desc: Reads the specified amount of sectors ahead of time to try to avoid later stalls. Affects both physical CD-ROM and CD images. 333000 will try to read the complete disk (requires an additional 750MB of RAM).

options.label: Dynamic Recompiler
options.desc: Dynamically recompile PSX CPU instructions to native instructions. Much faster than using an interpreter, but may be less accurate on some platforms.

options.label: PSX CPU Clock Speed (%)
options.desc: Overclock or under-clock the PSX CPU. Should be much less than 100 (something like 57) due to some real hardware slowdowns not being emulated. Usually should be left at 'Auto', else glitches or hangs are likely.

options.label: Dithering Pattern
options.desc: Enable emulation of the dithering technique used by the PSX to smooth out color banding artifacts. "Force" enables it even if the game turns it off. Increases performance requirements.

options.label: Threaded Rendering
options.desc: When enabled, runs GPU commands in a secondary thread. 'Auto' enables it if at least 2 CPU cores are detected.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Auto (Threshold)' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting. 'Fixed Interval' utilises the 'Frameskip Interval' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Auto (Threshold)', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: Frameskip Interval
options.desc: Specify the maximum number of frames that can be skipped before a new frame is rendered.

options.label: Display Internal FPS
options.desc: Show the internal frame rate at which the emulated system is rendering content. Note: Requires on-screen notifications to be enabled in the libretro frontend.

options.label: Display Informational Notifications
options.desc: Shows things like unsafe hack options that are enabled and the BIOS name that is booting.

options.label: Use fractional frame rate
options.desc: Instead of the exact 50 or 60 (maximum) fps for PAL/NTSC the real console runs closer to something like 49.75 and 59.81fps (varies slightly between hw versions). PCSX-ReARMed uses the former "round" framerates to better match modern displays, however that may cause audio/video desync in games like DDR and Spyro 2 (intro). With this option you can try to use fractional framerates.

options.label: Framebuffer readout
options.desc: Some games make changes to the framebuffer while it's being sent to the display, which is currently not emulated. However this option allows to choose if the emulator takes the video frame before the emulated PSX active display period ('Early') or after ('Late'). Normally this should be left at 'Auto'.

options.label: RGB32 output
options.desc: Improves color depth for true color modes (most FMVs and occasional title screens). Causes higher CPU usage due to double memory bandwidth requirement, even in 15bpp modes. Takes effect on game reload only (libretro limitation).

options.label: Hi-Res Downscaling
options.desc: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will be downscaled to 320x240 by skipping lines and/or columns. May be useful on some devices with native 240p display resolutions that lack efficient hardware scaling.

options.label: (GPU) Slow linked list processing
options.desc: Slower but more accurate GPU linked list processing. Needed by only a few games like Vampire Hunter D. Should be autodetected in most cases.

options.label: (GPU) Horizontal overscan
options.desc: The PSX can display graphics way into the horizontal borders, even if most screens would crop it. This option tries to display all such graphics. Note that this may result in unusual resolutions that your device might not handle well. The 'Hack' option is intended for the widescreen hacks.

options.label: (GPU) Screen centering
options.desc: The PSX has a feature allowing it to shift the image position on screen. Some (mostly PAL) games used this feature in a strange way making the image miscentered and causing uneven borders to appear. With 'Auto' the emulator tries to correct this miscentering automatically. 'Game-controlled' uses the settings supplied by the game. 'Manual' allows to override those values with the settings below.

options.label: (GPU) Manual position X
options.desc: X offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Manual position Y
options.desc: Y offset of the frame buffer. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Manual height adjustment
options.desc: Height adjustment. Only effective when 'Screen centering' is set to 'Manual'.

options.label: (GPU) Show Interlaced Video
options.desc: When enabled, games that run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) will produced interlaced video output. While this displays correctly on CRT televisions, it will produce artifacts on modern displays. When disabled, all video is output in progressive format. Note: there are games that will glitch is this is off.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution
options.desc: Render games that do not already run in high resolution video modes (480i, 512i) at twice the native internal resolution. Improves the fidelity of 3D models at the expense of increased performance requirements. 2D elements are generally unaffected by this setting.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Speed Hack
options.desc: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Improves performance but reduces compatibility and may cause rendering errors.

options.label: (GPU) Enhanced Resolution Texture Adjustment
options.desc: ('Enhanced Resolution' Hack) Solves some texturing issues in some games in Enhanced Resolution mode. May cause a small performance hit.

options.label: Audio Reverb Effects
options.desc: Enable emulation of the reverb feature provided by the PSX SPU. Can be disabled to improve performance at the expense of reduced audio quality/authenticity.

options.label: Sound Interpolation
options.desc: Enable emulation of the in-built audio interpolation provided by the PSX SPU. 'Gaussian' sounds closest to original hardware. 'Simple' improves performance but reduces quality. 'Cubic' has the highest performance requirements but produces increased clarity. Can be disabled entirely for maximum performance, at the expense of greatly reduced audio quality.

options.label: CD Audio
options.desc: Enable playback of CD (CD-DA) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include CD audio, at the expense of missing music.

options.label: XA Decoding
options.desc: Enable playback of XA (eXtended Architecture ADPCM) audio tracks. Can be disabled to improve performance in games that include XA audio, at the expense of missing music.

options.label: Show Input Settings
options.desc: Show configuration options for all input devices: analog response, Multitaps, light guns, etc. Quick Menu may need to be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Analog Axis Bounds
options.desc: Specify range limits for the left and right analog sticks when input device is set to 'analog' or 'dualshock'. 'Square' bounds improve input response when using controllers with highly circular ranges that are unable to fully saturate the X and Y axes at 45 degree deflections.

options.label: Rumble Effects
options.desc: Enable haptic feedback when using a rumble-equipped gamepad with input device set to 'dualshock'.

options.label: DualShock Analog Mode Toggle Key Combo
options.desc: When the input device type is DualShock, this option allows the emulated DualShock to be toggled between DIGITAL and ANALOG mode like original hardware. You can select the button combination for this.

options.label: Multitap Mode
options.desc: Connect a virtual PSX Multitap peripheral to either controller 'Port 1' or controller 'Port 2' for 5 player simultaneous input, or to both 'Ports 1 and 2' for 8 player input. Mutlitap usage requires compatible games.

options.label: NegCon Twist Deadzone
options.desc: Set the deadzone of the RetroPad left analog stick when simulating the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers. Used to eliminate drift/unwanted input.

options.label: NegCon Twist Response
options.desc: Specify the analog response when using a RetroPad left analog stick to simulate the 'twist' action of emulated neGcon Controllers.

options.label: Mouse Sensitivity
options.desc: Adjust responsiveness of emulated 'mouse' input devices.

options.label: Player 1 Lightgun Crosshair
options.desc: Toggle player 1's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

options.label: Player 2 Lightgun Crosshair
options.desc: Toggle player 2's crosshair for the Guncon or Konami Gun. Only works if RGB32 output is off (video options).

options.label: Konami Gun X Axis Offset
options.desc: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Konami Gun Y Axis Offset
options.desc: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Konami Gun (Hyper Blaster / Justifier) device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon X Axis Offset
options.desc: Apply an X axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon Y Axis Offset
options.desc: Apply a Y axis offset to light gun input when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon X Axis Response
options.desc: Adjust relative magnitude of horizontal light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Guncon Y Axis Response
options.desc: Adjust relative magnitude of vertical light gun motion when emulating a Guncon device. Can be used to correct aiming misalignments.

options.label: Instruction Cache Emulation
options.desc: Enable emulation of the PSX CPU instruction cache. Improves accuracy at the expense of increased performance overheads. Required for Formula One 2001, Formula One Arcade and Formula One 99. [Interpreter only; partial on lightrec and ARM dynarecs]

options.label: Exception and Breakpoint Emulation
options.desc: Enable emulation of some almost never used PSX's debug features. This causes a performance hit, is not useful for games and is intended for PSX homebrew and romhack developers only. Only enable if you know what you are doing. [Interpreter only]

options.label: Turbo CD
options.desc: This makes the emulated CD-ROM extremely fast and can reduce loading times in some cases. Warning: many games were not programmed to handle such a speed. The game (or even the emulator) MAY CRASH at ANY TIME if this is enabled.

options.label: Disable CPU/GTE Stalls
options.desc: Will cause some games to run too quickly. Should be disabled in almost all cases. Interpreter only.

options.label: System Region
options.desc: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL'/'Europe' is 50hz while 'NTSC'/'US' is 60hz. Games may run faster or slower than normal (or produce errors) if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Master System Type
options.desc: Choose which type of hardware (SMS or Game Gear) the core should emulate when running Master System content.

options.label: Master System ROM Mapping
options.desc: Choose which ROM mapper the core should apply. 'Auto' will work for a wide range of content, but in some cases automatic detection fails.

options.label: Master System Palette in TMS modes
options.desc: Choose which colour palette should be used when an SMS game runs in one of the SG-1000 graphics modes.

options.label: Sega CD RAM Cart
options.desc: Emulate a Sega CD RAM cart, used for save game data. WARNING: When enabled, internal save data (BRAM) will be discarded.

options.label: Core-Provided Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core Provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: LCD Ghosting Filter
options.desc: Apply an image 'ghosting' filter to mimic the display characteristics of the Game Gear and 'Genesis Nomad' LCD panels.

options.label: Video Renderer
options.desc: Specify video rendering method. 'Accurate' is slowest, but most exact. 'Good' is faster, but fails if colors change mid-frame too often. 'Fast' renders the complete frame in one pass, and is incompatible with games that rely on mid-frame palette/sprite table updates.

options.label: Audio Sample Rate (Hz)
options.desc: Higher values increase sound quality. Lower values may increase performance. Native is the Mega Drive sound chip rate (~53000). Select this if you want the most accurate audio.

options.label: FM filtering
options.desc: Enable filtering for Mega Drive FM sound at non-native bitrates. Sound output will improve, at the price of being noticeably slower

options.label: Master System FM Sound Unit
options.desc: Enable emulation of the SMS FM Sound Unit. This produces higher quality audio in some games, but non-Japanese titles may fail to run.

options.label: Mega Drive FM chip type
options.desc: Select the Mega Drive/Genesis FM chip type. Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis mostly used YM2612, which produced a distinct distortion. YM3438 was used in model 2 consoles.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Enable a low pass audio filter to better simulate the characteristic sound of a Model 1 Mega Drive/Genesis. Note that only Model 1 and its add-ons (Sega CD, 32X) employed a physical low pass filter.

options.label: Low-Pass Filter %
options.desc: Specify the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Input Device 1
options.desc: Choose which type of controller is plugged into slot 1. Note that a multiplayer adaptor uses both slots.

options.label: Input Device 2
options.desc: Choose which type of controller is plugged into slot 2. This setting is ignored when a multiplayer adaptor is plugged into slot 1.

options.label: Dynamic Recompilers
options.desc: Enable dynamic recompilers which help to improve performance. Less accurate than interpreter CPU cores, but significantly faster.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: No Sprite Limit
options.desc: Removes the original sprite-per-scanline hardware limit. This reduces flickering but can cause visual glitches, as some games exploit the hardware limit to generate special effects.

options.label: 68K Overclock
options.desc: Overclock the emulated 68K chip. Can reduce slowdown, but may cause glitches.

options.label: Video Scale (Restart)
options.desc: Set internal video scale factor. Increasing the scale factor improves the appearance of the internal 'Dot Matrix' LCD filter.

options.label: 60Hz Mode
options.desc: Update the display at 60Hz instead of the native 72Hz Pokemon Mini's refresh rate by dropping every sixth frame. Reduces video smoothness, but avoids screen tearing on displays that do not support native operation above 60Hz.

options.label: LCD Filter
options.desc: Select internal screen filter. 'Dot Matrix' produces an LCD effect that mimics real hardware. LCD filters are disabled when 'Video Scale' is set to '1x'.

options.label: LCD Mode
options.desc: Specify the greyscale 'color' reproduction characteristics of the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Analog' mimics real hardware. '2 Shades' removes ghosting, but causes flickering in most games.

options.label: LCD Contrast
options.desc: Set contrast level of emulated liquid crystal display.

options.label: LCD Brightness
options.desc: Set brightness offset of emulated liquid crystal display.

options.label: Palette
options.desc: Specify palette used to 'colorize' the emulated liquid crystal display. 'Default' mimics real hardware.

options.label: Piezo Filter
options.desc: Use an audio filter to simulate the characteristics of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

options.label: Low Pass Filter
options.desc: Enables a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound of the Pokemon Mini's piezoelectric speaker.

options.label: Low Pass Filter Level (%)
options.desc: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Screen Shake Level
options.desc: Enable virtual force feedback effect by 'shaking' the screen.

options.label: Controller Rumble Level
options.desc: Enable physical force feedback effect via controller rumble.

options.label: Turbo Button Period
options.desc: Specify the repeat interval (in frames) when holding down the Turbo A button.

options.label: Internal Palette
options.desc: Enables colorization of Supervision games.

options.label: LCD Ghosting
options.desc: Simulates LCD ghosting by blending pixels from multiple successive frames. Can help to alleviate the flickering that is common in Supervision games.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Skip frames to avoid audio buffer under-run (crackling). Improves performance at the expense of visual smoothness. 'Auto' skips frames when advised by the frontend. 'Manual' utilises the 'Frameskip Threshold (%)' setting.

options.label: Frameskip Threshold (%)
options.desc: When 'Frameskip' is set to 'Manual', specifies the audio buffer occupancy threshold (percentage) below which frames will be skipped. Higher values reduce the risk of crackling by causing frames to be dropped more frequently.

options.label: CPU Core
options.desc: CPU emulation backend: Dynarec (JIT) is fastest, IR Interpreter is more compatible, Interpreter is slowest but most accurate.

options.label: Fast Memory
options.desc: Unstable.

options.label: Ignore Bad Memory Accesses
options.desc: Silently ignores invalid memory reads/writes instead of erroring; keeps buggy games running.

options.label: I/O Timing Method
options.desc: How disc I/O timing is emulated: Fast for speed, Host-accurate, or Simulate UMD delays for realism.

options.label: Force Real Clock Sync
options.desc: Slower, less lag.

options.label: Locked CPU Speed
options.desc: Overrides the emulated PSP clock; higher can boost frame rates, lower can fix speed-sensitive games.

options.label: Memory Stick Inserted
options.desc: Some games require ejecting/inserting the Memory Stick.

options.label: Cache Full ISO in RAM
options.desc: Loads the entire ISO into RAM to cut load stutter, at the cost of higher memory use.

options.label: Internal Cheats Support
options.desc: Enables PPSSPP's internal cheat-code (CWCheat) support.

options.label: Game Language
options.desc: 'Automatic' will use the frontend language.

options.label: PSP Model
options.desc: Emulated PSP hardware model; PSP-2000/3000 has more RAM, which some homebrew/games use.

options.label: Backend
options.desc: 'Automatic' will use the frontend video driver. Core restart required.

options.label: Software Rendering
options.desc: Slow, accurate. Core restart required.

options.label: Rendering Resolution
options.desc: Core restart required with Vulkan.

options.label: MSAA Antialiasing
options.desc: Vulkan only. Core restart required.

options.label: Crop to 16x9
options.desc: Remove one line from top and bottom to get exact 16:9. Core restart required with Vulkan.

options.label: Frameskip
options.desc: Renders only every Nth frame to keep speed on slow hardware, at the cost of visual smoothness.

options.label: Frameskip Type
options.desc: Whether the frameskip value means a fixed number of frames or a percentage of target FPS.

options.label: Auto Frameskip
options.desc: Automatically skips frames only when needed to hold full speed.

options.label: Render Duplicate Frames to 60 Hz
options.desc: Can make framerate smoother in games that run at lower framerates.

options.label: Detect Frame Rate Changes
options.desc: Notify frontend.

options.label: Buffer Graphics Commands
options.desc: GL/Vulkan only, slower, less lag, restart.

options.label: Confirmation Button
options.desc: Which face button confirms in menus (Cross or Circle), matching regional PSP conventions.

options.label: Analog Circle vs Square Gate Compensation
options.desc: Compensates for square-gate analog sticks so diagonals map correctly to the PSP's circular range.

options.label: Analog Deadzone
options.desc: Additional deadzone to apply after frontend input.

options.label: Analog Axis Scale
options.desc: Additional sensitivity factor to apply after frontend input.

options.label: Skip Buffer Effects
options.desc: Faster, but nothing may draw in some games.

options.label: Skip GPU Readbacks
options.desc: Some games require GPU readbacks, so be careful.

options.label: Lazy Texture Caching (Speedup)
options.desc: Faster, but can cause text problems in a few games.

options.label: Spline/Bezier Curves Quality
options.desc: Only used by some games, controls smoothness of curves.

options.label: Lower Resolution for Effects
options.desc: Reduces artifacts.

options.label: Hardware Transform
options.desc: Offloads vertex transform to the GPU for speed; disable only to fix rare rendering issues.

options.label: Software Skinning
options.desc: Combine skinned model draws on the CPU, faster in most games.

options.label: Hardware Tesselation
options.desc: Uses hardware to make curves.

options.label: Texture Upscale Type
options.desc: Algorithm used to upscale textures: xBRZ, Hybrid, Bicubic, or Hybrid+Bicubic.

options.label: Texture Upscaling Level
options.desc: CPU heavy, some scaling may be delayed to avoid stutter.

options.label: Texture Deposterize
options.desc: Fixes visual banding glitches in upscaled textures.

options.label: Texture Shader
options.desc: Vulkan only, overrides 'Texture Scaling Type'.

options.label: Anisotropic Filtering
options.desc: Sharpens textures viewed at steep angles; higher levels look better with minor GPU cost.

options.label: Texture Filtering
options.desc: Texture sampling mode: Auto, Nearest (sharp/blocky), Linear (smooth), or Auto max quality.

options.label: Smart 2D Texture Filtering
options.desc: Gets rid of some visual artifacts caused by unnecessary texture filtering in some 2D games, by switching to nearest filtering.

options.label: Texture Replacement
options.desc: Loads custom high-res replacement textures from disk when available for a game.

options.desc: Enables emulated Wi-Fi/networking for ad-hoc multiplayer; beta and can break some games.

options.desc: Uses UPnP to auto-open router ports for online ad-hoc multiplayer.

options.label: UPnP Use Original Port ('ON' = PSP compatibility)
options.desc: Maps the PSP's original network ports via UPnP for compatibility with real-PSP peers.

options.label: Port Offset ('0' = PSP compatibility)
options.desc: Shifts emulated network ports by this amount to avoid conflicts when running multiple instances.

options.label: Minimum Timeout (Override in ms, '0' = default)
options.desc: Overrides the minimum network timeout in ms; '0' uses the default.

options.label: Forced First Connect (Faster connect)
options.desc: Forces the first ad-hoc connection attempt to speed up matchmaking.

options.label: Color Depth (Restart)
options.desc: Specifies number of colors to display on-screen. 24-bit may increase performance overheads on some platforms.

options.label: Audio Filter
options.desc: Enables a low pass audio filter to soften the 'harsh' sound produced by the Atari 7800's TIA chip.

options.label: Audio Filter Level
options.desc: Specifies the cut-off frequency of the low pass audio filter. A higher value increases the perceived 'strength' of the filter, since a wider range of the high frequency spectrum is attenuated.

options.label: Dual Stick Controller
options.desc: Maps Player 2's joystick to the right analog stick of Player 1's RetroPad. Enables dual stick control in supported games (e.g. Robotron: 2084, T:ME Salvo).

options.label: Console Region (Reload Core)
options.desc: Specify which region the system is from. 'PAL' is 50hz, 'NTSC' is 60hz. Games will run faster or slower than normal if the incorrect region is selected.

options.label: Preferred Aspect Ratio
options.desc: Choose the preferred content aspect ratio. This will only apply when RetroArch's aspect ratio is set to 'Core provided' in the Video settings.

options.label: Crop Overscan
options.desc: Remove the borders at the top and bottom of the screen, typically unused by games and hidden by the bezel of a standard-definition television. 'Auto' will attempt to detect and crop the ~8 pixel overscan based on the current content.

options.label: Hi-Res Blending
options.desc: Blend adjacent pixels when game switches to hi-res mode (512x448). Required for certain games that use hi-res mode to produce transparency effects (Kirby's Dream Land, Jurassic Park...).

options.label: Blargg NTSC Filter
options.desc: Apply a video filter to mimic various NTSC TV signals.

options.label: Audio Interpolation
options.desc: Apply an audio filter. 'Gaussian' reproduces the bass-heavy sound of the original hardware. 'Cubic' and 'Sinc' are less accurate, and preserve more of the high range.

options.label: Allow Opposing Directions
options.desc: Enabling this will allow pressing / quickly alternating / holding both left and right (or up and down) directions at the same time. This may cause movement-based glitches.

options.label: SuperFX Overclocking
options.desc: SuperFX coprocessor frequency multiplier. Can improve frame rate or cause timing errors. Values under 100% can improve game performance on slow devices.

options.label: Reduce Slowdown (Hack, Unsafe)
options.desc: Overclock SNES CPU. May cause games to crash! Use 'Light' for shorter loading times, 'Compatible' for most games exhibiting slowdown and 'Max' only if absolutely required (Gradius 3, Super R-type...).

options.label: Reduce Flickering (Hack, Unsafe)
options.desc: Increases number of sprites that can be drawn simultaneously on screen.

options.label: Randomize Memory (Unsafe)
options.desc: Randomizes system RAM upon start-up. Some games such as 'Super Off Road' use system RAM as a random number generator for item placement and AI behavior, to make gameplay more unpredictable.

options.label: Block Invalid VRAM Access
options.desc: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be disabled for correct operation.

options.label: Echo Buffer Hack (Unsafe, only enable for old addmusic hacks)
options.desc: Some homebrew/ROM hacks require this option to be enabled for correct operation.

options.label: Show Light Gun Settings
options.desc: Enable configuration of Super Scope / Justifier / M.A.C.S. rifle input. NOTE: Quick Menu must be toggled for this setting to take effect.

options.label: Light Gun Mode
options.desc: Use a mouse-controlled 'Light Gun' or 'Touchscreen' input.

options.label: Super Scope Reverse Trigger Buttons
options.desc: Swap the positions of the Super Scope 'Fire' and 'Cursor' buttons.

options.desc: Enables the SNES graphic clip/window effects; disabling can help debug hidden layers.

options.label: Enable Transparency Effects
options.desc: Enables SNES transparency/color-blending effects; disable to debug or for a harder look.
